data.review_body:
Reply to AliExpress Choice Customer Service

Thank you for proving my point with this exact copy/paste standard reply.

You ask for my order number via your form? The case is ALREADY fully documented inside your own system with photos, video evidence and chat logs. Asking me to start over proves you haven't even read the case. This is not customer service, it's delay tactics.

Let's talk about your policy for damaged goods:
1.  You require the customer to return a broken/defective item to China AT THE CUSTOMER'S OWN EXPENSE. A return shipment often costs more than the product itself. Your policy is intentionally designed to make customers give up.
2.  You demand endless photo and video proof, but even with crystal clear evidence you still reject the claim.
3.  You violate EU and Norwegian Consumer Law. In Norway we have a 2-year right to complain for manufacturing defects. The SELLER is responsible for return costs for defective goods. Your policy illegally puts all risk and cost on the buyer.

This is not "not the experience we want you to have". This IS your business model.

 This is exactly why people should shop at local stores in Norway - No dropshipping, fast delivery from Norway, and a real warranty that actually works. Like many stores.
I've will actually start a company in Norway.

I will never shop at AliExpress again until you change this system that punishes honest customers.

Order is documented under Order: 
- 3075958315468217
- 3075754382158217
- 3075472362948217
- 3075039686638217

 - Everything is there if you actually bother to look.

 Stop with the copy/paste bot replies. You already have all documentation in your dispute system.

Your damaged goods policy is: Received a broken item? Pay $40 shipping yourself to return a $15 item to China. That's not a return policy, that's a scam designed to make customers give up.

 Under Norwegian law, the seller must cover return costs for defective goods. You are violating consumer law.
 This reply only proves my review is 100% correct.

`This case will also be reported to Forbrukertilsynet (Norwegian Consumer Authority) and ECC Norway for violating EU consumer rights.

extrêmement déçu par AliExpress. J’ai reçu un article défectueux et non conforme à la description de l’annonce. Malgré les preuves fournies et mes explications, AliExpress refuse de procéder à un remboursement intégral et me propose seulement un remboursement partiel. 22 euros pour 80 euros 

Ce qui est particulièrement incompréhensible, c’est que je n’ai pas reçu le produit correspondant à ce qui était présenté et vendu. Lorsque l’article est défectueux et non conforme à la description, il est normal de demander le remboursement total.

J’ai pourtant essayé de régler le problème de manière amiable, mais le service client reste inflexible et ne semble pas prendre réellement en compte les éléments fournis.

Très mauvaise expérience : produit non conforme, défectueux et remboursement refusé en totalité. Je trouve cette façon de traiter les clients particulièrement décevante.

Je déconseille fortement de faire confiance à AliExpress si vous rencontrez un problème avec une commande et que vous attendez une prise en charge sérieuse

Ich kämpfe jetzt seit Wochen mit dem AliExpress-Support wegen eines defekten, sperrigen Laufbands. Die Plattform zwingt mich in einem automatisierten Support-Kreislauf dazu, das riesige Gerät bei einem lokalen UPS-Paketshop abzugeben. Jeder, der auch nur fünf Minuten nachdenkt (oder meine Fotos gesehen hat), weiß, dass ein normaler Kiosk-Paketshop ein solches Großgerät niemals annehmen kann und wird – und UPS lehnt die Annahme vor Ort logischerweise rigoros ab.
​Trotz unzähliger Beweise, Fotos und Erklärungen wird man im Minutentakt mit stumpfen Standard-Textbausteinen abgespeist. Der Gipfel der Absurdität: Selbst wenn man öffentlich auf Kritik reagiert, kommen Ausreden wie angebliche "Ziffernfehler" bei Bestellnummern, nur um das Problem weiter verschleppen zu können.
​Wer hier sperrige Elektronik oder Fitnessgeräte bestellt, wird im Schadensfall komplett im Stich gelassen. Null Sterne, wenn das möglich wäre – absolut inkompetenter Support!

data.review_body:
For over seven years, I was a loyal and frequent customer of AliExpress. However, my most recent experience exposed the reality of their customer service and supposed buyer protection, permanently ending my relationship with the platform.

The Issue:
I purchased an item for €20. When it arrived, it did not match the product description at all. I promptly opened a dispute, providing clear photos and videos documenting the discrepancy.

The Unacceptable Support Response:
* Customer service demanded that I return the item at my own expense, which would cost €100 in international shipping—five times the value of the item itself.
* They offered store coupons instead of a monetary reimbursement to cover the return shipping costs, which was completely unreasonable.
* I escalated the matter over ten consecutive times trying to reach a fair resolution, but only received automated replies, stalling, and a total disregard for buyer protection.

Resolution:
When it became evident that AliExpress would not resolve the issue, I filed a chargeback dispute directly through my bank. I submitted all supporting evidence, including photos, videos, and chat transcripts.
* The bank initiated a 21-day review period.
* After 21 days, my money was fully refunded, backed by EU consumer and banking protections, without any assistance from AliExpress.

As soon as the refund was settled, I permanently deleted my account and decided never to use the service again.

Advice for Buyers:
If a platform refuses to address a legitimate issue, remember that local consumer protection laws and bank dispute mechanisms (particularly within the EU) hold international sellers accountable. Do not hesitate to file an official bank dispute with proper documentation.
data.review_headline: My Disappointing Experience with AliExpress After 7 Years: Protected by Law, Not Customer Service

data.review_body:
Quiero denunciar públicamente el desamparo total y la estafa consentida que estoy sufriendo por parte de AliExpress España en los pedidos 3075461165118982 (máquina de 164,40€) y 3075598217988982 (extensión de 34,47€).El vendedor ha duplicado a conciencia la misma etiqueta en ambas disputas para engañar al sistema informático. Esa etiqueta pertenece exclusivamente a la extensión. Al estar clonada en la disputa de la máquina, que mide 62 cm, Correos sí admitiría ese paquete individual y yo perdería automáticamente los 164,40€. Mientras tanto, la trampa de la etiqueta duplicada imposibilita usarla en la extensión por superar las medidas de un metro (mide 1,08 metros según las fotos de medición oficiales de Correos que tengo), provocando que esa disputa se cierre a favor del vendedor al ser físicamente imposible devolverla por incompatibilidad de los productos. Si uso esa etiqueta fraudulenta, la estafa queda completada y pierdo el dinero de ambos pedidos.Su soporte automático ignora de forma sistemática los dossiers en PDF que he adjuntado con las fotos de la báscula oficial de Correos y las cintas métricas, respondiendo únicamente con largas. El equipo superior me ha contestado hoy en ambos casos exigiéndome cerrar las disputas y abrir unas nuevas, lo cual es una trampa informática a sabiendas, ya que es IMPOSIBLE abrir una nueva disputa en esos pedidos una vez que se cierra.He grabado un vídeo continuo sin cortes desde mi casa donde se demuestra en directo la estafa de que siempre me asignan la misma etiqueta clonada en la pantalla del ordenador y en el bulto físico. Todo el contenido gráfico, el vídeo sin cortes y las capturas de su soporte avalando el fraude están publicados íntegramente de forma pública en el hilo oficial de Forocoches y en mi cuenta de Twitter/X (@Yolanda85571266) para que cualquier potencial cliente vea cómo funciona su protección al comprador de verdad. Exijo el reembolso inmediato de mis 198,87€ y la aplicación de sus propias políticas de fraude.

ACTUALIZACIÓN 04/09/2026: ¡MÁXIMA VERGÜENZA! Vuestra respuesta de "investigar en 48 horas" es una plantilla falsa para lavar vuestra imagen pública. Simultáneamente, vuestro sistema informático me acaba de responder DENTRO de la disputa exigiéndome que CANCELE la reclamación o use la etiqueta clonada que Correos rechaza porque el paquete mide 1,08 m (límite 1 m). Es una coacción informática para dejarme indefenso, porque si cierro la disputa ya NO se puede volver a abrir. No voy a picar. El caso ya está en el Centro Europeo del Consumidor (Expediente: ECCES-84271). ¡Exijo soluciones reales de humanos, no bots!

Odpowiedź na publiczną odpowiedź AliExpress

AliExpress twierdzi, że próbował się ze mną skontaktować, ale nie otrzymał odpowiedzi i nie ma pewności, czy ich wiadomości do mnie dotarły.

TO NIEPRAWDA.

Od kwietnia 2026 roku AliExpress wysłał do mnie około 20 wiadomości e-mail. Odpowiedziałem na wszystkie. Dodatkowo sam wysłałem co najmniej 26 wiadomości e-mail z pełną dokumentacją.

Przekazałem między innymi odpowiedzi z banku, potwierdzenie nadania i odbioru zwróconego produktu, informacje dotyczące rzekomego zwrotu oraz dowody potwierdzające, że bank nie blokuje zwrotu.

Kontaktowałem się również przez czat AliExpress, Facebooka i Instagram. Łącznie prób kontaktu było prawdopodobnie około 300.

Mimo tego AliExpress publicznie twierdzi, że nie otrzymał ode mnie odpowiedzi.

To jest absurdalne i niezgodne z faktami. Problem nie polega na braku kontaktu z mojej strony, ale na tym, że AliExpress ignoruje przedstawione dowody i wysyła w kółko te same automatyczne odpowiedzi.

ALIEXPRESS UKRADŁ PIENIĄDZE!!! UWAGA!!!!

23 marca 2026 r. kupiłem w sklepie Anbernic na AliExpress konsolę Anbernic RG VITA Pro za 740,48 zł.

15 kwietnia 2026 r., zaledwie 6 dni po otrzymaniu produktu, złożyłem oświadczenie o odstąpieniu od umowy i poinformowałem o tym sprzedawcę.

SPRZEDAWCA MA MÓJ PRODUKT, A JA NIE MAM ANI PRODUKTU, ANI PIENIĘDZY.

AliExpress nieustannie odsyła mnie do banku

Po każdym zgłoszeniu otrzymuję praktycznie tę samą odpowiedź:

Please contact the dispute and charge back department of the bank or payment channel to confirm the refund with the refund voucher.

BANK NIE BLOKUJE ŻADNEGO ZWROTU.

700,45 zł – Zwrot nie powiódł się

oraz:

„Zwrot pieniędzy nie powiódł się z nieprzewidzianych przyczyn. Aby uzyskać pomoc, skontaktuj się z działem obsługi.”

Najgorsza obsługa klienta, z jaką miałem do czynienia

Kontaktowałem się setki razy przez różne kanały.

Mimo to wciąż otrzymuję te same automatyczne odpowiedzi, a teraz AliExpress publicznie twierdzi, że nie odpowiedziałem na ich e-maile.

To po prostu nieprawda.

Pieniędzy nie otrzymałem.

SCAM - AVOID AT ALL COSTS

I ordered a 4TB external hard drive, but the real capacity tested was only 63GB! The controller identified is a "ChipsBnk Flash Reader," a cheap USB flash drive chip that's been rigged. The drive only weighs 65g, while a real 2.5" hard drive weighs 130-200g minimum: this isn't a hard drive at all, just a disguised USB stick. On top of that, it's completely unusable: impossible to format, whether through Windows or diskpart (clean, create partition, convert mbr, exFAT, FAT32 - all fail).

Delivery was also a disaster: the courier first cancelled claiming flooding, even though it hadn't rained for months. Then he gave me only 40 minutes to travel 10km to meet him myself, with no regard for my schedule.
A product that lies about its capacity, is unusable, and had a disastrous delivery. Dispute and refund request opened.

data.review_body:
Update – 4 September 2026:
AliExpress publicly replied to this review saying they had “launched an investigation” and would contact me within 48 hours.
The result of that “investigation” was an email demanding that I obtain a formal quality inspection report from a recognised third-party institution such as BV, TÜV or CCIC, or from a certified repair provider, to prove that the defect was not caused by “human factors”.
This is absurd.
This is not a cheap disposable charger. It is a high-power 380W desktop charger that failed within the advertised 1-year warranty period. The seller has already agreed to replace it once returned. My only unresolved request is that the reasonable international return postage for that agreed warranty replacement be covered or reimbursed.
Instead of resolving that simple issue, AliExpress has repeatedly moved the goalposts.
I have provided multiple videos, photos, warranty evidence and seller correspondence. Their escalation team repeatedly sent generic “insufficient evidence” responses without explaining what was actually missing. I was then asked to provide another detailed video, which I did. Now they are demanding a professional third-party inspection report that could easily cost more than the product itself.
I have never dealt with any major retailer or online platform selling into Australia that makes a warranty claim this difficult.
The support process itself is also badly fragmented. Live chat, the case page and email do not appear to share information properly. I repeatedly had to confirm my email address, was told to reply to emails I never received, and eventually had to use Google Drive and third-party image hosting just to submit evidence.
This is not customer support. It is obstruction.
AliExpress may be fine for cheap items where you are prepared to write off the purchase if something goes wrong. I would not trust the platform for higher-value electronics or anything where warranty support actually matters.
If Trustpilot allowed 0 stars, that is what I would give AliExpress for this warranty experience.

data.review_body:
Je tiens à exprimer mon indignation la plus totale face aux méthodes inacceptables d'AliExpress.
​Suite à un rappel officiel de produit défectueux émis par la plateforme elle-même, j'ai accepté le remboursement de mon achat. Au lieu de recréditer automatiquement la carte bancaire utilisée lors du paiement, le service client exige que je remplisse un formulaire en ligne comportant l'ensemble de mes données bancaires ultrasensibles (notamment le code IBAN, SWIFT et des informations personnelles privées).
C'est une violation manifeste de la sécurité des données et une pratique abusive intolérable. Demander à un client de livrer ses coordonnées bancaires complètes via une simple interface non sécurisée, alors qu'il est victime d'un produit défectueux retiré de la vente, ressemble fort à une tentative de phishing institutionnalisé ou à une collecte illégale de données personnelles.  Je dénonce publiquement ces méthodes indignes d'un site de e-commerce qui bafouują les droits et la sécurité de ses clients.
data.review_headline: Pratiques abusives, non-remboursement et exigence illégale de données bancaires sensibles par AliExpress

data.review_body: Soy un comprador habitual y compro desde el 2012, vamos que 14 años comprando. Al principio era fenomenal, los precios muy baratos y freeshipping, aunque fallaba el proceso de devolución y era arcaico eran ciertamente permisivos. Me hicieron dos feos que hoy en dia recuerdo, hice varios pedidos que llegaron en un solo paquete que se perdió o se devolvió a origen de unos 17 euros, perdí la apelación porque pedian pruebas que no podía darle porque obviamente no habia recibido nada y los de la oficina de correos no me daban nada a pesar de pedirselo, ahí perdi los 17 euros y no recibí nada a cambio pero al poco tiempo devolví un producto de 87€ y sin querer presioné que me lo devolvieran al banco que cerré, justo a posteriori les pedi por chat de soporte y llamada que lo dieran en bono, pues no hicieron ni p** caso ya que su servicio al cliente es pésimo y lamentable, pues luego tuve un problemón porque ni aliexpress ni el banco se hicieron responsables, el banco me decía que ellos devolvían automáticamente las transferencias al comerciante y Aliexpress se lavaba las manos diciendo que ellos habían transferido el dinero pero NO verificaban si lo habian recibido de vuelta, estuve dos meses contactando con Aliexpress de forma constante (más de 15 veces), después explicar a cada uno de nuevo y de mucho inútil suelto conseguía de vez en cuando que enviaran la apelación a una """instancia superior""" que es gente con un puesto jerárquico más alto que no hace nada más rascarse los huevos y no verificar absolutamente nada. Ahora ya no solo juegan con el scam de las monedas que no sirven de nada y te hace creer que puedes tener descuentos con ellas y ganar premios (mentira) es solo para que pases más tiempo en la aplicación sino que ahora los supuestos cargos de aduanas de 3€ te dicen que los descuentan pero que te los añaden a los "gastos de importación" 🤦🏻 e incluso han endurecido bastante las políticas de devolución, son unos sinvergüenzas de mucho cuidado. Seguiré comprando porque a veces necesito cosas específicas que solo se pueden conseguir en esta aplicación pero con pies de plomo y compro mucho mucho menos de lo que hacía antes. En fin.. Una vergüenza, todavía sigo con el rencor de los 100€ euros que me han robado.

data.review_body: This is the 2nd time I've done business w/ AliExpress, and it will probably be the last. Last time, they dropped off my package outside of my apartment complex. The only reason I received it is because a neighbor rescued it before it was stolen. This time, they sent it to a different address altogether. It's been a nightmare tracking it down. AliExpress was of no help whatsoever. I was stuck with their so-called "AI" canned response chat-box which had me repeating my answers over and over again, with no solution. I finally got ahold of a human Gofu rep who showed me where to see a photo of my package -- something AliExpress and it's tracking company were not able to do -- which confirmed what I suspected: the idiot driver delivered the package to the wrong address. Gofu said it would take them up to 10 days to resolve the issue, which means I get to go knocking on strangers' doors to get my package back. This is totally unacceptable. If AliExpress cannot deliver packages to their customers, they should shut-down their website and sell their product out of the back-end of a jeep.

data.review_body:
Experiencia muy decepcionante con AliExpress y su gestión de la garantía

Llevo varios días intentando reclamar a AliExpress por una televisión que compré hace aproximadamente ocho meses y que ha dejado de funcionar correctamente. Considero que el producto debería estar cubierto por la garantía correspondiente, pero conseguir simplemente que atiendan mi reclamación se está convirtiendo en una auténtica odisea.

Dispongo del número de pedido y de toda la información relacionada con la compra. El pago se realizó mediante PayPal y también conservo los correos electrónicos y demás documentación que acredita la operación. Incluso tengo comunicaciones de AliExpress relacionadas con el envío y con el pedido, por lo que no entiendo qué dificultad existe para localizar y verificar una compra que está perfectamente identificada.

He contactado con el servicio de atención al cliente en numerosas ocasiones y he abierto varios casos. El problema es que cada vez que consigo hablar con una persona diferente recibo una respuesta distinta. Un agente me indica una cosa, otro me pide una información diferente y, después de varios intercambios de correos, directamente han dejado de responderme.

Lo que estoy reclamando no es algo extraordinario: simplemente quiero que se gestione la garantía de una televisión comprada hace unos ocho meses. Tengo el número de pedido, puedo acreditar el pago realizado mediante PayPal y conservo documentación relacionada con la compra. Aun así, llevo días intentando conseguir una solución sin obtener una respuesta clara.

Estoy totalmente decepcionado con la experiencia. No entiendo cómo puede ser tan complicado tramitar una garantía cuando el cliente aporta la información necesaria para identificar la compra. Lo peor de todo no es solamente que el televisor haya dejado de funcionar, sino la sensación de estar completamente abandonado por el servicio de atención al cliente después de haber comprado el producto en su plataforma.

He tenido que abrir varios casos, repetir la historia una y otra vez y explicar constantemente la misma situación a diferentes personas. Y ahora, después de varios contactos, ni siquiera obtengo respuesta.

Me parece una forma muy frustrante de tratar a un cliente que simplemente está intentando hacer valer la garantía de un producto comprado en la plataforma.

Por todo ello, mi valoración de la experiencia con AliExpress es actualmente muy negativa. Espero que alguien de la empresa lea esta reseña y se ponga en contacto conmigo para solucionar de una vez el problema. No estoy buscando ningún trato especial: únicamente quiero que mi reclamación sea atendida y que se me dé una solución clara y coherente.

Después de tantos días intentando solucionar algo que debería ser relativamente sencillo, me siento completamente decepcionado y muy frustrado con AliExpress.

data.review_body:
I have been a loyal AliExpress customer for years and used to have great experiences, but this company has completely degraded. What was once a reliable online store has now turned into a platform that buyers should strictly avoid.

Here is the exact timeline of events:

July 1, 2026: I placed an order for a motorcycle accessory (Order ID: 3074451372473930, Tracking: LV102309322UZ).

August 13, 2026: I fulfilled 100% of my buyer duties by emailing all required official bank statements and invoice receipts directly to Montenegro Customs/Post.

August 30, 2026: The AliExpress system explicitly displayed a written guarantee: "Guaranteed for delivery by 2026-08-30. If it doesn't arrive by this date, you're entitled to a full refund."

August 31, 2026: The package was still NOT delivered. I requested a refund based on their written guarantee.

The Problem:
Instead of honoring their own policy, AliExpress dispute management blindly rejected my refund request claiming "insufficient proof."

I submitted full evidence showing that I completed all required customs paperwork weeks ago and that the package was never delivered. AliExpress completely ignored the provided evidence, ignored their own passed deadline, and shifted logistics failures onto me.

It is NOT the buyer’s job to chase logistics or postal delays after submitting all clearance documents. AliExpress failed to deliver on time, broke its written refund policy, and is withholding my money.

After years of smooth shopping, I am deeply disappointed by how terrible their customer service and business ethics have become. Avoid this platform at all costs.
data.review_headline: AliExpress Breached Written Guarantee & Refuses Refund

data.review_body:
Compré un Mini PC anunciado con Intel i9 y 16 GB de RAM. Desde el primer día, el equipo y el monitor estaban ARDIENDO día y noche. El PC ejecutaba minería oculta en la sombra: me fundía UNA PILA DIARIA en el ratón inalámbrico hasta que lo quemó, y me frió la placa base de mis altavoces Logitech de 40€. Dos controladores de seguridad del sistema se mostraban dañados debido a este malware.
Les envié capturas de pantalla de la descripción del sistema y de los controladores dañados, pero ignoraron todo el material visual. Pusieron excusas baratas y me exigieron vídeos absurdos de la caja de embalaje y de las piezas solo para lavarse las manos. AliExpress se conchabó con la tienda obligándome a cerrar la disputa a cambio de una miseria de devolución. Aún tenía la cara dura cuando me queje de decirme que no me daban la devolución completa " porque el pc que me quedaba aún valía para algo"! ( Tengo sus emails)
Al formatear e instalar Windows limpio de Groupon, saltó el pastel: el procesador real es un Intel i3 viejo. Hoy he abierto el chasis con herramientas de precisión y el zoom del móvil ha destripado la cochambre: la tarjeta de memoria física es un frankenstein de desguace con chips Micron código FBGA D9QBQ (referencia MT41K1G4RH-107:E). ¡Son solo 4 GB de tipo DDR3L vieja! Los chips tienen las letras borradas y vienen con pegotes de cola rancia tapados por software pirata para engañar al sistema. No voy a parar hasta formalizar la denuncia por fraude en consumo (OMIC). Ladrones
ACTUALIZACIÓN (Pedido 3074606425985300):
En su resolución final me escribieron que les parecía justo el reembolso de 82€ (acordado a mis espaldas con la tienda estafadora que ya desapareció) porque consideraban que el aparato aún se podía utilizar. Esto es falso: jamás existió un "acuerdo mutuo". Su soporte pactó de manera unilateral a mis espaldas basándose en conversaciones sesgadas, ignorando mis tres disputas legítimas posteriores donde aporté todas las fotos exigiendo el reembolso total.
Respecto a su cínica petición de "nuevas evidencias": ¿Qué esperan que les envíe? ¿Quieren una fotografía de la placa base quemada y fundida de mi altavoz Logitech? ¿Una foto de un ratón dañado que devora una pila al día por la sobretensión? ¿O acaso quieren la tarjeta de memoria RAM "Frankenstein" oculta dentro del aparato? Una tarjeta vieja, usada y manipulada de forma delictiva, con los chips pegados literalmente con pegotes de pegamento, unos boca arriba y otros boca abajo, para engañar al sistema y dar 4 GB reales en lugar de los 16 GB prometidos. Una auténtica aberración técnica.
Su sistema ya está saturado con todas las imágenes, vídeos y capturas que les envié. Tienen registrado perfectamente cómo el sistema operativo mostraba datos falsificados de hardware y cómo venía trucado el equipo con un Windows falso lleno de malware de minería. He tenido que gastar mi propio dinero en comprar módulos de RAM legítimos Crucial, adquirir una licencia limpia de Windows 11 de mi propiedad y dedicar más de 100 horas de trabajo técnico para neutralizar el peligro eléctrico y de seguridad de este aparato en mi hogar. El coste total está valorado en más de 500 euros. No voy a seguir enviando archivos que ustedes ya poseen. Si un supervisor humano no asume la responsabilidad de este fraude, entregaré el dossier completo a la Policía Nacional (Delitos Tecnológicos) y a la OMIC para proceder por la vía legal.
Atentamente - Cliente, o sea yo.
Nueva respuesta de AliExpress hoy pidiendo más vídeos y mi réplica pública definitiva:
Anuncio abiertamente que NO voy a seguir enviando más vídeos ni imágenes. Su contestación pidiendo "evidencias adicionales" es una farsa corporativa para quedar bien ante el público. Su sistema YA POSEE todas las pruebas de las disputas anteriores. Tienen en sus servidores las capturas donde el propio Windows avisaba de que había dos controladores de seguridad totalmente dañados que fue imposible recuperar ni a través de Intel, debido al malware oculto del sistema de fábrica. Asimismo, ya disponen de mi descripción detallada sobre el fraude físico de la RAM y de los daños materiales de mis periféricos. Se niegan a revisarlo de forma humana.
Por otra parte, desde el día de esta reclamación, extrañamente estoy sufriendo un acoso indecente de llamadas perdidas muy cortas (tres/cuatro segundos) de números desconocidos (anteayer recibí 5, ayer recibió 8 llamadas hasta las 20:30 de la noche, hoy ya van 4). Me resulta extraño ya que en este número rara vez recibo llamadas spam. No voy a atender ninguna llamada telefónica de números extraños. Solo atiendo números con registro oficial y trazables. Si no revisan de oficio su propio historial para asumir el fraude comercial y los daños, el caso se resolverá directamente por la vía policial y judicial.

data.review_body:
I originally gave AliExpress 1 star, increased it to 2 stars because they appeared to finally be paying attention to my complaint, and gave them the benefit of the doubt.

I now regret doing that.

After AliExpress told me that my case had been escalated, I waited SEVEN DAYS for them to deal with it.

After all that time, I received this response:

"As you did not raise any dispute, we are unable to support your refund request."

That is the latest excuse.

And it is particularly infuriating because it comes after weeks of AliExpress repeatedly asking me for evidence.

Let's recap what has actually happened.

I purchased an IPL device on 1 December 2025.

It worked normally for approximately eight months and then failed. It still powers on and the modes can be selected, but it produces no IPL flashes whatsoever.

The manufacturer's manual states a 12-month warranty.

I contacted the seller.

The seller repeatedly told me they would resolve the problem and contact me.

They didn't.

I contacted AliExpress.

AliExpress repeatedly asked me for photographs, a description and video evidence.

I provided them. Multiple times.

They then told me the case had been escalated.

I waited seven days.

And now they have suddenly decided that because I "did not raise any dispute", they cannot support my refund request.

Seriously?

If this was always going to be the reason for refusing the claim, why did AliExpress repeatedly ask me for videos and other evidence?

Why did they allow me to repeatedly provide that evidence?

Why did they escalate the case?

Why did nobody tell me at the beginning that they would refuse to consider the matter on this basis?

And most importantly:

Why has nobody actually addressed the 12-month warranty?

This is what makes the whole experience so incredibly frustrating.

Every time I answer one of their requirements, another obstacle appears.

First it was:

"Your order is over six months old. Provide evidence."

I provided the evidence.

Then they asked for the video again.

I provided a new video.

Then they said the case had been escalated.

I waited seven days.

Now it is:

"You did not raise a dispute."

At no point have they actually addressed the fundamental issue:

A product with a stated 12-month warranty failed after approximately eight months, and I have provided clear evidence of the fault.

Instead of dealing with that warranty claim, I appear to be going around in circles while AliExpress finds another procedural reason not to deal with it.

I have been patient. I have cooperated. I have supplied the evidence they requested. I have waited through their escalations.

My patience has now run out.

I am returning this review to 1 star.

This is not what I consider customer service.

I will continue to document this case and update this review if AliExpress finally decides to properly address the warranty claim.

AliExpress: I am not asking you for special treatment. I am asking you to explain why a product that failed within its stated 12-month warranty is apparently not being covered — and to stop moving the goalposts every time I satisfy your latest request.

Order: 8206749627449967.
data.review_headline: Back to 1 star – Seven-day "escalation" results in another excuse not to honour the warranty

⭐ -000/5 Stars - Seller Refused to Ship + AliExpress Customer Care is Useless 

My Experience:
I ordered a product from AliExpress. After payment, the seller REFUSED to ship the order and admitted it. 

I have all the evidence. The seller speaks confidently, claiming he didn't send me the product, as if he knew AliExpress was on his side. No respect for the law or the customer. 

I contacted AliExpress Customer Care 3 times asking for compensation for my losses: 
1. Bank processing fees
2. Currency conversion fees 
3. Lost discount coupons that I cannot get back 

Instead of helping, AliExpress sent me the EXACT SAME copy-paste bot reply 3 times:
"We will penalize the seller... the order will be canceled and refund will be issued automatically." 

They completely ignored my request for compensation. 

The Problem:
A simple refund does NOT cover the damage caused by their seller. I lost money AND time because of AliExpress and their seller. But AliExpress policy is: "Just wait for auto-cancel". No responsibility. 

Customer Service:
0/10. No human. No solution. No escalation. Just bots. When I threatened to post on Trustpilot they still ignored me. 

Conclusion:
Do NOT order from AliExpress if you value your time and money. If the seller scams you, AliExpress will do nothing except return your money and let you pay the bank fees. 

 Update 

Your response was like a robot again, it won't solve any problems. You didn't address how I'll be compensated for the losses you caused me.
That's the most important thing now. A refund isn't a solution for me. The seller was confident they'd get what they wanted, and now you're siding with them. I wasted time, fees, and vouchers. In the end, I only get the price of the product. Is that really fair? This is nonsense.


final update: WORST Experience Ever - Scam + Biased Customer Service - 00000 Star

My experience with AliExpress was absolutely terrible.

I placed an order and paid the full amount with coupons. The seller openly refused to ship. 
I contacted AliExpress Customer Service expecting "Buyer Protection"... I was wrong.

Customer Service was the WORST I have ever dealt with:
1. They FORCED me to cancel the order instead of punishing the seller.
2. They were 100% biased towards the seller and accused me that my order "did not include taxes" and demanded proof for something that was clear from the start.
3. In the end, they auto-closed the order with no solution and no compensation.

The Result:  
I lost over $12 in coupons and discounts  that took me months to collect. Plus fees bank 
On top of that, I received less money back due to currency conversion fees that they refused to refund.  
The seller lost nothing. I lost time and money.

Final Verdict:  
AliExpress provides ZERO buyer protection. It's all fake promises.  
How can sellers NOT scam people with a policy this biased?  
I strongly advise everyone to AVOID buying from AliExpress.  
I lost my money and my trust in them.

#AliExpressScam #WorstCustomerService

#BadCustomerService

Ordered some magnets and acrylic gloss for my 3d projects on august 16th. The products had a fast guaranteed delivery date of august 28th, which has come and gone as they arrived today on the 30th. I went online and asked where my coupons were to which I was sent a preprepared paragraph saying they didnt qualify. When I asked why and sent a snip from my order online, I was then asked by the agent, could you please send a copy of the whole order, what???  

First, how do you tell me that the orders dont qualify when you havent even checked into it, it sounds like they fight the guarantee every order. Well, we can send to the higher ups and you'll get an answer in 2 -3 days, what??? What answer, it was guaranteed fast delivery, why isnt it instant, it is with TEMU, I said fine Ill just send the product back and never order again, what do i hear after that from the agent, oh, we'll have to send that to the higher ups also. 

ALI has no credibility and is unethical. I tried again because some of the products are unique but this is the last time I get burnt

REPLY TO ALI: I have already chatted with 3 agents who tell me I am not eligible for the fast delivery coupon even though the deliveries were 2 days past the guarantee.  I gave each agent the order ID and a screen of the guarantee from the orders. Why they would need more than a item description and order ID is beyond me.  

Everytime something is delivered late, which is 90% of the time, I have to fight for a lousy dollar. 

Im done with Ali, im just returning the products and items that are still being delivered. It's not worth waiting over 2 weeks for an order and then the drama and stress to have to fight with Ali to get them to honor their guarantee.

My advice to anyone reading this, use Temu. $5 guarantee and they are late maybe 5%, and you dont fight over the fast guarantee, it's automatically delivered

I would give less than 1 star if I could.
I wanted to return 2 items I ordered (glassware) and started a return, I started 2 returns and realised it would make sense to put these on 1 return label. The prompt told me to cancel my return request and then add both items to a new return. Problem started now, being unable to cancel, it then said to contact customer support. Which I did, the Agent (person not AI) said that the ALSO could not cancel my request, and gave no reason why. They insisted on me sending both back and sticking both labels on the return. This seemed impossible to me & I mentioned that Aus post would not process that package with 2 return labels. They said this would be forwarded to a 'specialist' team to make sure my items arrived and to confirm that X2 returns were inside the origional box. They advised I take a video of me boxing 2 glasses into the origional box in case of verification at a later stage.
Next day I posted the items, Aus post would only allow 1 label (as I assumed and flagged as a problem) once I got home I started another Agent chat to confirm the situation I was in was understood and that this would be sent to whoever is 'inspecting'the items on arrival. Upon inspection they will see, X2 items and be able to process the second return. 
This Agent understood my issue and also flagged a 'specialist'team to contact me. 

The specialist team requested video /photo evidence of the boxing, which I sent, also a weight of the item, which Aus post never did (nor was I told to on my end) The conversation feeds with all agents disappears after the 'end chat' so other than a couple of screenshots I was unable to 'prove'what they said to me.
Currently I now have no glassware and they have denied me a refund. This was the response from the specialist team, insufficient evidence. The warehouse has literal proof of the items in their possession. How that is not evidence is beyond me. Hollow sympathy with zero willingness to help me. I followed their instructions and now have no product and no money. This is stealing. 
The inspection would clearly show a discrepancy in the return item, having more than the item under the return. Either they do not inspect items, or they are hiding behind beurocratic tape to willingly screw their customers. Disgraceful experience & complete waste of time trying to get them to do the right thing.

Le 5 juillet 2026, AliExpress a répondu publiquement à mon précédent avis en affirmant qu'un « représentant dédié » traitait mon dossier par e-mail en raison de sa « complexité ». Aveu explicite de fraude : Le vendeur (RouExpress Navi Store) a admis noir sur blanc dans la messagerie officielle que les puces CPU et la mémoire RAM de l'appareil livré sont défectueuses et non conformes, précisant même que son propre fournisseur l'avait indemnise pour ce défaut.

Complicité d'AliExpress : Malgré la preuve irréfutable de cet aveu de culpabilité transmis au litige, AliExpress refuse de faire appliquer la protection des acheteurs et protège un vendeur malhonnête.

Tromperie sur Trustpilot : Leurs réponses aux avis négatifs ne sont que de la poudre aux yeux destinées à rassurer les futurs acheteurs. En privé, il n'y a aucun suivi, aucun représentant dédié et aucun remboursement.

AliExpress cautionne sciemment la vente de matériel non conforme et ment ouvertement dans ses réponses publiques. Ne vous laissez pas avoir par leurs formules de politesse robotisées. Exigez le remboursement intégral.

data.review_body:
Order number: 1121706383388373

The item arrived with poor build quality and defective, misaligned drawers, so I opened a dispute.

AliExpress instructed me to return the product to an address in Bremen, Germany. Because the parcel was around 30 kg, normal postal return services could not handle it. I repeatedly asked AliExpress for a proper return label or practical solution, but all I received were generic and automated replies.

I eventually arranged the return myself through Eurosender/UPS and paid EUR 146.95 for shipping. AliExpress had also told me that the return shipping cost would be reimbursed.

The return was delayed because UPS needed a German contact number. I contacted AliExpress multiple times asking for help, but again received no useful assistance. AliExpress then closed the dispute while the parcel was still in transit.

The package was ultimately successfully delivered in Bremen on 25 August, and UPS provided proof of delivery. I sent AliExpress the shipping label and proof of delivery, exactly the type of evidence they had previously requested.

Despite this, AliExpress has now explicitly refused to return my money, without giving any proper reason.

So the situation is simple: the seller has the returned cabinet, AliExpress refuses to refund my DKK 1,863.18, and I am also still owed the EUR 146.95 return shipping cost.

The worst part is the customer service. No matter how much evidence I provide, I mostly receive automated replies that do not address the actual issue.

I would strongly advise against buying expensive or bulky items from AliExpress. If something goes wrong, you may return the product successfully and still have AliExpress refuse to give your money back.

Update: AliExpress has now refunded the DKK 1,863.18 purchase price for the cabinet, so that part of the complaint has finally been resolved.

However, the issue is not fully resolved yet.

I paid EUR 146.95 to return the defective cabinet through Eurosender/UPS because the parcel was around 30 kg and the normal return options were not suitable. AliExpress had previously confirmed that the return shipping cost would also be reimbursed.

So I appreciate that the cabinet refund has now been processed, but I am still waiting for reimbursement of the EUR 146.95 return shipping cost.

I will update this review again once the remaining amount has been refunded.
data.review_headline: AliExpress refuses to refund me even after receiving the returned item

Bought two items from AliExpress. One arrived within a week, was exactly as described, and the shipping was very fast. The other showed the same estimated delivery date but ended up arriving three weeks later.

By that point, I needed the item urgently, so I had already bought another one locally. I then tried to return the AliExpress item, and that’s where the real headache started.

The entire returns process seems deliberately complicated. Half the time, the system doesn’t work properly, and you have to jump through hoops just to get the return accepted. Eventually, I managed to send it back to the vague address they provided, but the address doesn’t even appear to be recognised on the courier’s tracking system.

I submitted all the required information and proof, only to be told they can’t find the return.

Honestly, save yourself the time and hassle. If something goes wrong, the returns process is an absolute nightmare. Avoid AliExpress like the plague.

data.review_body:
Der AliExpress-Kundenservice scheint nicht darauf ausgerichtet zu sein, Probleme zu lösen, sondern vielmehr darauf, sie so kompliziert und ermüdend zu machen, dass Kunden irgendwann aufgeben.

Der Verkäufer hat schriftlich bestätigt, dass zwischen dem von mir bestellten und dem tatsächlich gelieferten Produkt eine Abweichung besteht, und dies als „Fabrik-Druckfehler“ erklärt. Trotzdem verlangt AliExpress weiterhin ein Unboxing-Video, obwohl ich vor der Lieferung niemals darüber informiert wurde, dass ein solches Video erforderlich ist.

Damit nicht genug: Nun verlangt AliExpress zusätzlich, dass ich das Produkt professionell oder in einem Labor auf das verwendete Material testen lasse. Dies, obwohl der Verkäufer bereits schriftliche Erklärungen zum Produkt abgegeben hat und die wesentlichen Punkte meines Streits dokumentiert sind.

Ständig neue, möglicherweise kostenpflichtige oder zuvor nicht angekündigte Nachweise zu verlangen, wirkt nicht wie der Versuch, ein Kundenproblem zu lösen. Es vermittelt vielmehr den Eindruck, dass der Kunde so lange belastet und ermüdet werden soll, bis er schließlich aufgibt.

Nun bin auch ich müde und habe genug davon.

Ein Kunde sollte nicht einen derart komplizierten und frustrierenden Prozess durchlaufen müssen, nur damit eine nachvollziehbar dokumentierte Reklamation überhaupt sachlich geprüft wird.

Diese Erfahrung hat mein Vertrauen in AliExpress vollständig zerstört. Ich werde nie wieder bei AliExpress einkaufen und werde auch andere Menschen über diese Erfahrung informieren, bevor sie sich für einen Kauf auf dieser Plattform entscheiden.

Shortly after placing my  order to the store called "Practical Tool 47 Store" (ID:912216240) on the AliExpress platform, I received a cryptic message from the store keepers offering me to send another version of the product I ordered, a cheaper, less features, but it was hard to understand, they also did not propose a compensation for the price difference.
Ordered: ESP32-S3-RS485-CAN-U
What I believe they meant: a clone of the ESP32-S3-RS485-CAN.

Msg: "Dear customer, do you mind if we switch to another product to ship to you? The functions are the same but the antenna installation method is different. Looking forward to your reply~"

It took them three full days to kind of answer in the meanwhile I was annoyed by their AI chatbot.
The answer was again unclear, and looking more and more like a scram.
I contacted AliExpress CS to discuss the situation, a case was escalated, the answer: this time we will take note of your comment... not much from that side.

At the time of writing this review the Store change the product labels and remove the genuine Waveshare reference for "onboad/external antenna"... this is most likely a clone but at the same price (even more expensive compared to the official Waveshare store, which unfortunately cannot ship easily to my address)...

After 8 days the Store cancelled my order, without my consent, without consulting me first, a refund is one the way from AliExpress, hopefully it will reach me in the coming days, but with the 2% extra fees from my bank I lost about 4% of the invoice amount... this is annoying to say the least.

The worse might be the last message from the Store:
"It doesn't matter, we have finished stocking, we will still order it according to your order, thank you~
Dear Customer, We have accepted your refund request. Pls check your account later. The refund will transfer to your account soon. Have a nice day! Best regards"

Again: I never asked for a refund, but to have my initial order fulfilled professionally.
I let you judge.

This Store is rated: Brand+ and Certified Original by the platform, for me this is a shame.

Even worse is that the product in question is still presented in the same way. It says a lot about how Aliexpress accept intentionally misleading product presentations. Alléchée par un prix défiant toute concurrence je suis retournée sur la plateforme d'Aliexpress que je ne fréquentais plus depuis longtemps. Suite à cet achat j' ai constaté que l'adresse d'expédition était une adresse périmée. Ils ne m'ont pas laissé de choix non plus au moment de l'achat et ont choisi cette adresse de manière arbitraire! Je ne l'ai vue qu'une fois l'achat fait. J' ai essayé de changer l'adresse immédiatement, le link n' a pas fonctionné. Ensuite, j' ai essayé d'annuler la vente, le link n' a pas fonctionné. J' ai donc contacté le service client et un agent m'a certifié qu'il procédait à l' annulation et que tout était bien annulé mais que cela prendrait 24h à être affiché. Peu avant minuit, un mail m'annonçant que les articles avaient été expédiés me met en alerte. Comment est ce possible ? Je recontacte le service client qui me répète en boucle que l'on ne peut rien faire car les produits ont été expédiés. J' explique que c'est entièrement de leur faute puisque un agent m'a assuré que la vente était annulée et que j' ai lâché l'affaire à ce moment-là faisant entièrement confiance à Aliexpress ! On m'a tout simplement menti pour que je cesse d'insister sur l'annulation de cette commande! Je ne travaille plus à cette adresse depuis deux ans, c'est un lieu public donc très gênant pour moi que l'on expédie à cette adresse. Il n' y a rien à faire, robots et agents humains répètent en boucle qu'une fois que la réception aura eu lieu, je serai remboursée. Autant expliquer la situation à un mur... Ils ont été incapables d'annuler la commande et m'ont menti au sujet de l'annulation, et refusent de rembourser avant la non livraison qui aura lieu dans un endroit public où les paquets sont déposés dans une boîte collective au nom de cet établissement (et non du mien) et qui apparaîtra comme livré alors que je ne peux le retirer puisque je n' y suis plus et que j' ai quitté la région. Une chose est sûre, cela me servira de leçon pour supprimer définitivement mon compte mais je ne lâcherai pas prise avant d'avoir eu raison de cause! 
"Nouvelle" réponse d'Aliexpress, zéro solution, ils répètent en boucle la même chose: ils tournent leurs clients en bourrique !
Évidemment ils répondent par mail et non pas dans la suite de ce message car ce serait bête de montrer sa mauvaise foi ici, voici donc leur mail de "nouvelle" réponse et "solution de conflit":
Cher client,

Nous vous remercions de nous avoir signalé ce problème. Veuillez accepter nos plus sincères excuses pour la gêne occasionnée.

Concernant la commande n° 3075800106286240, suite à votre demande, nous vous confirmons que le vendeur a déjà expédié votre colis, actuellement en transit. Nous regrettons de vous informer qu'il n'est plus possible de modifier l'adresse de livraison. Toutefois, nous vous proposons les options suivantes :

1. Contacter le transporteur : Dès l'arrivée du colis dans votre ville, vous pourrez contacter le transporteur afin de demander une livraison à une nouvelle adresse.
2. Refuser la livraison : Si nécessaire, vous pouvez refuser le colis. Veuillez noter cependant que le refus de livraison peut entraîner une déduction des frais de port pour le remboursement. Nous vous remercions de votre compréhension.

Nous vous remercions de votre compréhension. Si vous rencontrez d'autres problèmes lors de votre achat, n'hésitez pas à nous contacter par e-mail.

Cordialement,
L'équipe du service client AliExpress

data.review_body:
Je mets à jour mon avis pour préciser qu’AliExpress a finalement procédé au remboursement intégral de mes 359,04 €. Mais il aura fallu des semaines de démarches totalement disproportionnées pour obtenir le remboursement d’une commande que je n’avais jamais reçue.

Le suivi GLS comportait des informations incohérentes, indiquant notamment une livraison à Aulnay-sous-Bois, alors que le colis devait m’être remis dans un point relais du 20e arrondissement de Paris. Le point relais m’a confirmé n’avoir aucune trace du colis.

Malgré les très nombreux justificatifs fournis, AliExpress m’a renvoyé encore et encore vers GLS, en exigeant un document officiel de non-livraison. Or GLS m’a confirmé par écrit qu’il ne pouvait pas me fournir ce document et que c’était à l’expéditeur de les contacter directement.

J’étais donc enfermé dans une boucle absurde : AliExpress exigeait un document de GLS pour me rembourser, tandis que GLS expliquait que ce document devait être demandé par l’expéditeur.

Le vendeur Marketplace, Anbernic Europe Local Store, m’a ensuite proposé de m’expédier un nouvel exemplaire, reconnaissant ainsi qu'il existait bien un problème avec le premier envoi, mais sans accepter pour autant de me rembourser.

Le plus incroyable concerne le service client AliExpress lui-même. Une première fois, un conseiller m’a affirmé explicitement par messagerie qu’un remboursement intégral de 359,04 € avait été accordé et serait effectué sous 24 heures. C'était faux : aucun remboursement n'a suivi et je n'ai reçu aucun e-mail officiel de confirmation. Lorsque j'ai recontacté AliExpress, d'autres conseillers m'ont indiqué qu'ils n'avaient aucune trace de cet accord de remboursement ! J'ai alors été une nouvelle fois renvoyé vers GLS et sommé de produire le même document impossible à obtenir.

Il a donc fallu recommencer les démarches et obtenir une nouvelle escalade du dossier avant qu'AliExpress finisse réellement par valider puis effectuer le remboursement.

Entre-temps, j’avais dû multiplier les réclamations, fournir une attestation de non-réception, documenter l'absence du colis au point relais, effectuer un signalement SignalConso, déposer une plainte auprès de la police et envoyer une mise en demeure en recommandé avec l'ensemble du dossier (ce qui, soit dit en passant, m'a coûté environ 20 euros que je ne récupèrerai pas...).

Je reconnais donc qu’AliExpress m’a finalement remboursé les 359,04 € et je mets mon témoignage à jour pour le préciser.

Mais le remboursement final ne peut pas effacer la manière dont ce litige a été géré : semaines de démarches, réponses standardisées en boucle, services qui se contredisent, exigence répétée d’un document que le transporteur refuse de remettre au destinataire, et même annonce d’un remboursement sous 24 h qui n’existait manifestement pas dans leur système.

Le problème n'est finalement pas seulement qu'un colis puisse se perdre — cela peut arriver à n'importe quel commerçant. Le véritable problème est ce qui se passe chez AliExpress lorsque quelque chose tourne mal.

Après cette expérience, je ne commanderai plus jamais de produit de valeur sur AliExpress.

⭐ 1/5 malgré le remboursement final, en raison d’une gestion du litige que je considère absolument catastrophique.
data.review_headline: Il a fallu engager un véritable combat pour être remboursé (360 euros)

Ich habe über aliexpress am 3. August 2026 eine SSD Festplatte 16TB bestellt und geliefert bekommen.

Nachdem ich sie an meinem PC angeschlossen hatte wurde ich über Windows aufgefordert die Festlatte zu formatieren (15,34TB), was ich auch getan habe, soweit alles gut. Als ich dann so ca. 54GB Daten auf die SSD Festplatte übertragen hatte, kam irgendwann die Info dass diese Festplatte nicht aufzufinden sei und ich somit keinen Zugriff mehr auf die Festplatte hatte. 

Natürlich waren alle Daten unwiederbringlich verloren, was mich natürlich immens ärgert und mir ca. 500 Std. (a 20.-Euro) Arbeit zerstört hat. 

Da diese Festplatte nachweislich nicht die versprochene Kapazität hat und es bei AliExpress nachweislich massive Probleme mit Betrug von gefälschten Marken-SSDs und manipulierten Kapazitäten gibt haben sie mich als Kunde verloren.

data.review_body:
Poor-quality products, very slow delivery, inconvenient returns

1. Poor-quality products

I purchased nine products from AliExpress. Two of them,a miniature frying pan and a miniature knife, were so small and impractical that they looked more like children’s toy cookware than functional kitchen tools. Although the listings presented them as cookware suitable for frying eggs and preparing food, neither product was suitable for normal kitchen use. When my wife saw them, she could not help laughing because they looked like toys.

2. Very slow delivery

The delivery problems were widespread rather than isolated. One order took 14 days to arrive. Another took 16 days, with no tracking update for nearly seven days after August 20; I received a response only after I complained. Another shipment was marked as undeliverable because of "no access" but there was no known access problem at my address, and I received no notification or other indication that a delivery attempt had been made. I asked AliExpress to investigate what had happened, but no meaningful investigation or explanation was provided.

Most significantly, after purchasing only nine products, I received eight separate $1 coupons explicitly marked “Issued for late delivery.” AliExpress’s own records therefore confirm how frequently my purchases were delivered late.

3. Inconvenient returns

When I requested a return for the miniature frying pan, I submitted a photograph that clearly showed its extremely small, toy-like appearance. AliExpress nevertheless demanded extensive additional evidence, including a video of the packaging and product, close-ups of defects, a functional test, and records of communication with the seller.

Both the frying pan and the knife were unsuitable for normal use, but the return system appeared to allow only one product from the order to be returned. I may therefore be forced to keep and pay for another unusable item.

The $1 late-delivery coupons are also of little practical value because only one can be used per order. Using all eight would require me to place multiple additional orders and spend more money on AliExpress. These restrictions make both the return process and the supposed compensation unnecessarily inconvenient.

Update: AliExpress states in its public reply that it emailed me a “final solution.” However, the email I received did not resolve my complaint. It requested evidence again and stated that the seller would cover return shipping if the items did not match the listed dimensions.

I have already acknowledged that dimensions were listed. My complaint concerns product images that made the very small frying pan and knife appear much larger. I still have not received a clear answer on whether both items can be returned for a full refund with prepaid return shipping.

Sending an email is not the same as providing a resolution. My complaint remains unresolved.

Très mauvaise expérience – produit non conforme et service client décevant

J’ai commandé un kit de conversion pour vélo électrique clairement présenté comme « With 48V 18AH Battery », pour lequel j’ai payé 568,56 €. Or, j’ai reçu le kit sans la batterie, alors que le modèle livré coûte plus de 300 € de moins que celui que j’avais commandé et payé.

J’ai contacté le vendeur à plusieurs reprises afin qu’il m’envoie la batterie prévue dans ma commande. Malgré mes demandes, il a refusé de trouver une solution au problème.

J’ai donc ouvert un litige auprès d’AliExpress et fourni tous les éléments permettant de démontrer clairement la différence entre le produit commandé et celui qui m’avait été livré.

À ma grande surprise, AliExpress a rejeté ma demande sans fournir d’explication concrète et satisfaisante, alors que les preuves étaient pourtant parfaitement claires. AliExpress ne m’a accordé qu’un remboursement partiel de 85,28 €, alors que le produit reçu ne correspondait manifestement pas à celui que j’avais acheté.

J’ai finalement dû faire appel à PayPal. Après avoir examiné mon dossier et les preuves fournies, PayPal a accepté ma réclamation et m’a remboursé la somme restante. J’ai ainsi pu récupérer la totalité des 568,56 € que j’avais initialement payés.

Je suis extrêmement déçu, aussi bien par le vendeur que par la manière dont AliExpress a géré mon litige. Je m’attendais à un service client plus sérieux et, surtout, à une véritable protection du client lorsqu’un problème de conformité est aussi clairement documenté.

Je ne recommande absolument pas ce vendeur et, après cette expérience, je n’achèterai plus sur AliExpress.

Si vous décidez malgré tout d’acheter sur AliExpress, je vous conseille vivement de payer avec PayPal. Dans mon cas, c’est finalement PayPal qui m’a apporté la protection que je n’ai pas obtenue auprès d’AliExpress. Sans PayPal, je serais probablement resté avec un produit qui ne correspondait pas à ma commande et avec une perte financière importante.

Very disappointing experience – product not as described and extremely poor customer support

I ordered an electric bicycle conversion kit that was clearly advertised as “With 48V 18AH Battery” and paid €568.56. However, I received the kit without the battery, even though the version I received costs more than €300 less than the one I had ordered and paid for.
I contacted the seller several times and gave them every opportunity to correct the mistake by sending the battery included in my order. Unfortunately, the seller refused to resolve the problem.

I then opened a dispute with AliExpress and provided clear evidence showing the difference between what I had ordered and what I had actually received.
What happened next was extremely disappointing. AliExpress rejected my claim without providing any meaningful or convincing explanation, despite the evidence being clear. I was granted only a partial refund of €85.28, leaving me significantly out of pocket for a product that was not the one I had purchased.
I eventually had to turn to PayPal. After reviewing my case and the evidence, PayPal accepted my claim and refunded the outstanding amount, allowing me to finally recover the full €568.56 I had originally paid.
This experience has completely destroyed my confidence in AliExpress. I am particularly disappointed by the lack of customer protection and by the way my dispute was handled. When a customer receives a product that is clearly different from the one ordered and has documented evidence to prove it, I believe the platform should protect the customer rather than leave them to resolve the problem themselves.
I do not recommend this seller, and after this experience I will no longer purchase from AliExpress.
If you nevertheless decide to buy from AliExpress, I strongly recommend using PayPal as your payment method. In my case, PayPal provided the customer protection that I did not receive from AliExpress.

Why You Can No Longer Trust AliExpress Ratings! Bought a 97€ Dashcam on Ali, Got a Brick and a 19€ Refund! Hello everyone. I want to share a story about how AliExpress artificially maintains high ratings for scam sellers by depriving buyers of the opportunity to write the truth, and how their "arbitration" system works strictly in the seller's favor.  I bought a dashboard camera for my car, and it turned out to be completely defective. The GPS signal drops constantly, and the time zone resets all the time. The store sent me a firmware update, but it fails to install—the process gets interrupted, the dashcam reboots, and this loop keeps happening over and over, along with other issues regarding coordinates and software stability. I paid 97 euros for this device! While I was trying to figure out these issues with the store (which took about a month, if not more), I opened a dispute and requested a partial refund of 30 euros. AliExpress, however, decided that 19.44 euros would be more than enough for me, claiming that I was asking for too much money relative to these problems. The seller barely participated in the dispute; they rejected it only once, asking me to send data from the dashcam, which I did. After that, they took no further action and didn't contest anything else.I appealed the decision, but AliExpress stood its ground. They rushed to transfer the 19.44 euros almost on the exact same day, seemingly just to argue later that the money had already been refunded and nothing more could be done. That is exactly what happened, and those were the exact replies I received. Later on, the seller even confirmed that I was not to blame for the defects, acknowledged that I had received a partial refund, and offered me a 5-euro discount as compensation. For some reason, the refund amount shown on the seller's side was completely different—21.67 euros. The real catch happened when I wanted to leave a review after finishing all my testing and discussions with the seller. It turned out that the window of time to leave feedback is strictly limited. In my opinion, this is done intentionally so that people leave positive reviews before they even have a chance to properly test the product, preventing them from leaving an honest, negative one later. As a result, looking at all those filtered positive reviews, AliExpress's reputation remains untarnished. As I mentioned in another post, they encourage scammers by protecting them instead of fighting them. I have attached the screenshots regarding this case, some of which are in Russian.


Why You Can No Longer Trust AliExpress Ratings! Bought a 97€ Dashcam on Ali, Got a Brick and a 19€ Refund! / Почему больше нельзя верить рейтингам AliExpress! Купил регистратор на Али за 97€. Получил кирпич и возврат 19€!

Привет. Хочу поделиться историей о том, как AliExpress искусственно удерживает высокий рейтинг продавцов-мошенников, лишая покупателей возможности написать правду, и как их «арбитраж» работает в пользу продавца. 
Купил видео регистратор для машины, оказался не качественный, сигнал gps прерывается  постоянно, часовой пояс постоянно сбрасывается, магазин прислал прошивку она тоже не устанавливается, прерывается и видео регистратор перезагружается  и так кругом, ну и другие проблемы с координатами и так далее! Платил за регистратор 97 евро! Пока я выяснял проблемы регистратора с магазином (разбирался где то месяц если не больше)  я открыл спор и попросил частичный возврат 30 евро, на что aliexpress решил что мне хватит 19.44 евро, потому что по их подсчётам за эти проблемы я прошу слишком много денег, продавец не принимал участия в споре только один раз откинул его и попросил чтоб я прислал информацию с видео регистратора как я и сделал! Больше они участие не принимали и не чего не оспаривали!
Я оспаривал но АлиЭкспресс решил по своему, и очень быстренько перевел сумму 19.44, деньги мне перевели можно сказать в этот же день чтоб потом писать что они вернули мне деньги и больше не чего не могут сделать, так и было такие ответы я и получил!
Продавец тоже потом подтвердил что я в дефектах не виноват и  частичный возврат я получил и предложил мне скидку на 5 евро. У продавца сумма возврата почемуто была совсем другая 21,67 евро. Потом когда я хотел оставить отзыв о товаре после всех тестов и разбирательств с продавцом оказалось что отзыв можно оставить ограниченное время а по моему мнению это делается специально чтоб люди оставляли о товарах положительные отзывы не успев протестировать товар и не оставить правдивый отзыв!
И смотря на все положительные отзывы репутация АлиЭкспресс не портилась! Как я писал в другом посте они поощряют мошшеников помогая им и не борются с ними!

data.review_body:
I ordered an item on AliExpress, and the seller chose DPD as the courier for delivery. As most people in Europe know, that’s a bad idea to begin with, but I didn't have a choice in the matter. As ussual, DPD didn't deliver the package to my home and they even showed up at the drop-off point after closing time. DPD's "customer service" actually confirmed this. DPD then simply decided to return the item. This is clearly visible in the tracking details. I filed a complaint with AliExpress and submitted the tracking info as evidence, but the complaint was rejected due to a lack of proof. How else are you supposed to prove you didn't receive something? A photo of your empty hands? No more AliExpress thieves for me. TEMU is far more customer-oriented.

Update 28/08/2026:

After Writing the above review I was contacted again by AliExpress apologizing and informing me the purchase was refunded.  I do appreciate that.  However, I regret having to spend time writing a bad review in frustration, when this solution could have been given immediately.  I did not give any extra information additionally to when I first made the complaint.  Giving proof of not receiving the item should be enough for a refund, instead it is only given after writing a bad review.  AliExpress definitely still needs to work on their customer service!
data.review_headline: Update to: I ordered an item on AliExpress and it was never delivered

AliE moet dit onderzoek starten met PostNL, maar weigeren dit te doen. Naar meerdere keren contact te hebben gehad werd ik doorverwezen naar het zogenoemde sr team van AliE, maar dit maakt helemaal niks uit. Ze blijven stug de documenten opvragen bij mij die ik niet kan opvragen bij PostNL en proberen je van kastje naar de muur te sturen, zodat je opgeeft.

An diesem Lager scheint es keine Klingel zu geben, wenn dieses Lager überhaupt existiert unter dem Namen den mir aliexpress mitgeteilt hat. Jetzt habe ich die kaputte Lampe wieder zurückbekommen. data.review_body:
NUOVO AGGIORNAMENTO – Comunicazioni contraddittorie da AliExpress

Dopo aver inviato una formale diffida per il mancato rimborso di €105,69, ho ricevuto da AliExpress due comunicazioni completamente contraddittorie a distanza di pochi minuti.

Nella prima email mi viene comunicato che la mia richiesta è “in handling”, associata al work order n. 2053808660944605, e che devo attendere la risposta del relativo reparto.

Pochi minuti dopo ricevo invece una seconda comunicazione nella quale AliExpress afferma che non può approvare il rimborso, sostenendo che il prodotto restituito sarebbe diverso da quello acquistato.

La seconda risposta appare inoltre fortemente automatizzata e generata da un sistema AI, con una formulazione estremamente generica e senza alcuna risposta concreta alle contestazioni giuridiche e alle richieste specifiche contenute nella mia diffida.

Quindi quale sarebbe la posizione ufficiale di AliExpress? La mia pratica è ancora in gestione oppure è stata definitivamente respinta?

Continuano inoltre a basarsi sulle fotografie del magazzino, che non dimostrano che l’articolo fotografato fosse effettivamente contenuto nel pacco da me consegnato. Il tracking InPost dimostra invece che il pacco del reso è stato regolarmente consegnato.

Ho chiesto di verificare la situazione con InPost e di acquisire le evidenze oggettive della spedizione, in particolare i pesi registrati alla presa in carico e alla consegna, ma non ho ricevuto tali verifiche.

Mi aspetto quindi una risposta coerente, concreta e specificamente riferita alla mia contestazione, non comunicazioni automatiche contraddittorie.
data.review_headline: NUOVO AGGIORNAMENTO Comunicazioni contraddittorie da AliExpress

Website description inacurate. On 28th July I ordered red and blue car door trims from Shop1104091523.  The website states "Easy to Install and Maintain Simple to install on Car Door edges with no special tools required. The Item Length: 2M and Width: 0.8 cm ensure a precise fit for most applications". The website then shows pictures of how to fit including the removal of small steel strip. What I received was 0.5cm x 0.5cm and had no steel strips and the fitting instructions show measurements 10mm x 8mm. I have repeatedly requested a refund but they say "your recent return/refund request did not meet our evidence standards" despite the photographs of the items laying on a measuring tape and other photo's showing no steel strip and further photo's of what the website says.
28/8 received this mail Dear customer,

Thank you very much for contacting us. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused you.

We understand that you mentioned the item size does not match. After checking the product page, we found that the specifications are as follows:

Item Height: 1.1 cm/inch
Item Width: 0.8 cm/inch

We also noticed that your dispute has already been finished. If you are not satisfied with the dispute result, you may submit an appeal by clicking “Dispute Finished.” After that, please kindly upload a measurement video. We recommend making sure that the video clearly shows the measurement process and the relevant details, so the dispute team can review your case again.

Thank you very much for your understanding and cooperation.

I have already appealed and the pictures I sent included the item placed on a measuring tape showing they are 5mm also pictures showing there is no steel. I now question the need for a video is an AI delaying tactic to which I am unable to to do anyway. You are still advertising the item for sale please inspect it and you will see the measurements are not as you say nor is there any steel to remove. The pictures I sent clearly show all the evidence that you have not sent what is specified on the website.

data.review_body:
Be warned: Do Not Buy with AliExpress unless you want headaches. Do not Trust them!
I purchased an Executive Chair for an agreed Total = AU$757.91.  (AU$376.69 and an additional AU$312.32 for Shipping Costs. Tax  at AU$68.90)  The amount came out of my PayPal Account. For over a week the Seller wanted an additional AU$260.00 for shipping, whilst holding onto my money I already paid. I raised a concern with AliExpress. It was such a waste of time with AliExpress with the final statement from them stating Following an internal review of the information provided, we regret to inform you that the report has been deemed unsubstantiated. The reason for this decision is as follows:
The reported item/content does not violate platform regulations. The refunded my money in the end.

I cannot understand why AliExpress states that: "The reported item/content does not violate platform regulations" This response is quite concerning, and I do not understand why the ticket has been closed.

My primary concern is what prevents sellers from advertising products with a stated shipping fee, collecting payment from buyers, and then later claiming that additional shipping costs are required. Sellers should be responsible for maintaining accurate and up-to-date shipping charges before listing their products for sale. Buyers should not be placed in a position where they are forced to either pay more after the transaction or wait for a refund.

In this situation, the seller holds the buyer's funds while the matter is being disputed, potentially benefiting from access to that money during the process. Meanwhile, the buyer loses the opportunity to earn interest or otherwise use those funds. The seller can simply issue a refund at a later date without bearing any responsibility for the inconvenience, delay, or financial impact caused.

This does not seem fair or consistent with good business practices. It also raises concerns about making larger purchases through AliExpress in the future if the same issue can occur without consequence.

I believe sellers should be held accountable for providing accurate shipping costs and that buyers should receive compensation when errors arise due to the seller's failure to keep their shipping information current. In my view, the seller should bear the responsibility for this mistake, not the buyer.

Jusqu’à présent j’étais globalement satisfait, malheureusement tout a changé depuis quelques mois.
D’abord des rajouts de frais de douanes rendant les prix beaucoup moins attractifs, au moment de payer la commande. 
Mais ce n'est pas le seul problème, mes 4 dernières commandes ont eu des soucis de livraison.
La première, mon colis a été jeté sur le trottoir et je m'en suis rendu compte en sortant de chez moi, personne n'a sonné et la boite à lettre était à seulement 1 mettre de là où j'ai retrouvé le colis.
La deuxième, le colis a été marqué comme livré et je n'avais rien reçu, il y avait comme preuve de livraison des photos du colis (sans montrer l’environnement) et une fausse signature.
La troisième et quatrième, j'ai commandé un article destiné à un projet assez urgent, c’était début juin, après un moment, il à été marqué que le colis était bloqué pour défaut d’emballage, j'ai donc recommandé le 1er juillet, le même article étant donné que j'en avais absolument besoin pour finaliser mon projet. Le colis a mis 22 jours pour arriver en France. Bon c'etait long mais j'avais espoirs qu'une fois en France la livraison ce serait accélérée. Et bien non le colis est marqué dédouané, donné à la société de livraison, et plus rien, le colis n'a pas bougé depuis le 22juillet. Plus d'un mois après je me bas avec aliexpress pour être remboursé faute d’être livré. Personne n'est capable de me dire où se trouve mon colis, personne n'est capable de faire avancer ma livraison. Personne ne veut me rembourser. La seule chose qu'ils savent me dire c'est de les recontacter en octobre.... 4 mois de perdu et sans savoir, si un jour, je vais récupérer mon argent. 

Mise à jour suite à la réponse de Aliexpress :
J'ai effectivement reçu un mail d Aliexpress ... Me disant que mon cas  sera étudié, mais pas avant OCTOBRE, pour un article que j'ai commandé début juin... de grands mots, de grands discours pour pas grand chose derrière....
Je pense sérieusement qu'il faut fuir cette plateforme de vente, d'autres m'ont l'air bien plus sérieuses.

On ne vous demande pas de décrocher la lune ni de devenir le centre du monde, juste un truc tout bête : arrêtez deux minutes de nous prendre pour des buses !

Tenez vos engagements et remisez vos feintes grotesques pour esquiver les réclamations que vous réclamez vous-mêmes. C'est trop vous demander d'être juste décents ?

data.review_body:
This has turned into a giant scam. Do not buy anything expensive or important here.

As many other people say, you will end up with defective products.

When you complain about something that is not a visual defect, AliExpress declines the claim with the statement "We have carefully revisited all
the proof provided, including the newly updated proof and found that the proof is not effective enough to prove your claim."

There is no way of replying to these decisions, you have to start from an AI chat every time and fight your way to a frist line agent, then an appeal agent, which might be replying on email after up to a few months. 

From the time of their message, months later, you have exactly 24h until the case gets closed and you can no longer reply to the email. Then you start the process over.

I'm giving up now, to get my money back, and on AliExpress in general. This happened to me a few times on cheaper items, where I just ignored the loss. But this is the tipping point - there is no trust left.

Spend your money elsewhere! They protect the sellers and let them get away with shipping defect products. This also gets evident after you shop elsewhere. 75% of my last order on AliExpress was defective compared to a few percent on the other app I use.

There are other Chinese apps with magnitudes of better services and buyer protection. 

In other apps, you simply get free returns, on time per order. Simply return it if you don't like it. If it is clearly broken, others won't even ask you to return the product, just issue a refund.

Read other reviews, you will find the same story. Use another app and don't lose your money.
data.review_headline: This has turned into a giant scam
