data.review_body:
J’ai commandé un bac à pizza avec couvercle hermétique le 16 juillet 2026.
Le bac est arrivé comme prévu avec le couvercle, sauf qu’il n’est pas hermétique. Le couvercle est plus petit et se balade au niveau du haut du bac.
J’ai ouvert un litige auprès du service client et ce dernier m’a dit de voir avec le vendeur.
Le vendeur m’a proposé un remboursement partiel de 8$, puis après négociation, m’a proposé 10$.
Le vendeur m’a demandé de clôturer le litige pour procéder au remboursement. 
J’ai donc repris contact avec le service client et ce dernier m’a dit de ne pas clôturer le litige et qu’il s’en occupait.
Après plusieurs jours, et j’ai repris contact avec le service client, puisque je n’avais plus de nouvelles.
Ils m’ont demandé de transmettre les échanges de messages entre le vendeur et moi pour prouver l’accord. Le litige a traîné pendant plus d’un mois et après avoir eu plus de 15 interlocuteurs, j’ai pris contact par téléphone avec AliExpress où un agent m’a dit de clôturer le litige et d’en refaire un pour renvoyer le bac. 
J’ai donc clôturé et refais un nouveau litige pour avoir une nouvelle étiquette de retour, sauf que l’application AliExpress a planté et m’a fait un remboursement partiel.
J’ai passé des appels au service client et contacté par messages également, mais ils n’ont pas résolu le problème.
Le vendeur est un escroc, car après la clôture du litige, il n’a pas voulu honorer sa parole sur le remboursement des 10$ et le service client m’a induit en erreur et m’a menti à plusieurs reprises.
Ce site est une arnaque monumentale avec des vendeurs qui sont des escrocs et un service client malhonnête.
Je ne recommande pas du tout ce site chinois qui est malveillant.

Suite de ce dossier :

Le service client de AliExpress envoi des mails contradictoires et complètement malhonnête.
Il continu sur la même ligne, en disant qu’ils vont m’aider, qu’ils sont là pour régler le litige et envoie des mails pour dire qu’ils peuvent rembourser partiellement de 2€ et quelques centimes, puis d’autres mails ils disent qu’ils ne peuvent pas rembourser partiellement et quelques centimes si je veux renvoyer le bac, il faut que le vendeur soit d’accord. Or, le vendeur est un escroc notoire qui ne donne pas son aval pour le renvoi, les commentaires sur sa page parlent d’eux-mêmes, à savoir très négatifs. 
AliExpress continu d’être malhonnête dans ses démarches et je ne recommande pas du tout d’aller sur cette plateforme qui ne règle pas les litiges.

I’m genuinely starting to wonder whether anyone at AliExpress actually reads these reviews before responding, because your replies make it painfully obvious that you either haven’t read what I wrote, haven’t bothered checking the history, or simply don’t give two cents about what I’ve already told you.

You keep vomiting out the same recycled customer-service trash telling me to provide evidence and contact customer service, despite the fact that I have already provided the evidence and already dealt with your customer service repeatedly. How many times exactly am I supposed to provide the same information before someone at AliExpress actually reads it? Or do you need a translator?

At this point, your Trustpilot responses are nothing more than public copy-and-paste theatre. You slap another generic “we care about your satisfaction” paragraph underneath the complaint, pretend you've done something, and then send the customer straight back into the same ridiculous loop.

And the fact that you apparently aren’t even passing these reviews to the relevant team or person who can actually look at the case makes this even more pathetic. What exactly is the purpose of having a Trustpilot customer service response if nobody actually investigates the complaint behind it?

Maybe the next response can be a little more creative. Perhaps instead of the usual “Thank you for your patience, please contact customer service and provide evidence” routine, someone could actually read the complaint first — heck, even throw it into Google Translate if you're having trouble reading basic English. I know that might be an ambitious new concept for AliExpress, but surely it's worth trying.

Because right now it feels like your entire Trustpilot process is: Customer complains → AliExpress doesn't read complaint → AliExpress posts generic response → customer explains everything AGAIN → AliExpress doesn't read that either → repeat indefinitely. Congratulations, you've somehow turned customer service into an infinite loading screen.

Stop telling me to do things I have already done.

READ THE REVIEW. READ THE EVIDENCE. READ THE PREVIOUS RESPONSES. LOOK AT THE ACTUAL CASE. THEN DO SOMETHING ABOUT IT.

I don't need another AI-generated essay about how “committed” AliExpress is to resolving my issue. Your actions have demonstrated the exact opposite.

Every new response you post is just another excuse, another deflection, and another example of AliExpress completely failing to listen to the customer.

At this point, I honestly cannot tell whether I'm dealing with a customer-service department or an automated excuse generator — my money is on the latter.

And the most ridiculous part? You keep responding as though you're helping, when your responses themselves are becoming additional evidence of exactly what I'm complaining about. Keep posting these generic replies if you want — because every time you do, you're publicly demonstrating that AliExpress still hasn't bothered to understand or properly investigate the problem.

data.review_body:
If you are trying to buy anything off AliExpress, especially high value items, stop! The listings claiming the item are "In Stock" are almost entirely phantom inventory.

99% of the time these sellers do not actually have the physical item sitting in a warehouse. Instead, they operate as middlemen. They list it as available to boost their store’s search visibility. When you spend your money, they scramble to source it locally in China.

When they inevitably fail because the item is unavailable, they will message you asking you to cancel the order.

They do this because if they cancel it themselves, AliExpress severely penalizes their store. By making you cancel, they keep their seller metrics perfect while your money (in my case of dollars) is locked up for days in refund processing.

Save yourself the headache and frozen funds. Purchase through authorized, dedicated collectible retailers with transparent waitlists instead.
data.review_headline: DO NOT PURCHASE ANYTHING OF ALIEXPRESS

data.review_body:
Refund promised for months, endless copy-paste responses, no resolution

I ordered a Junsun 10" Android car radio (order #3073416525752010) which never arrived. AliExpress itself confirmed the refund and even shows a "Refund processed and submitted to the financial institution" status but the refund then shows as "Refund failed."

Since then I have been stuck in an endless loop with AliExpress customer service for months:

I have received the exact same automated email over 15 times, asking me to submit my bank details via the same link.
I have submitted my bank details more than 10 times, through the requested form, and directly in chat.
Every single chat agent (I've spoken to at least 8 different agents/bots under names like Abdelhamid, Dan, Vyn, Youmna, Mohamed) gives the identical scripted response: apologizing, asking for the same bank details again, and promising escalation to a "senior team" or "higher management."
I was told multiple times that my case was "escalated" and that I would hear back within 48 hours, then within 1-3 working days. Each time, the follow-up was the same template message asking for bank details all over again proving no one had actually reviewed my case.
A "senior team response" was logged in the system, which turned out to be the same copy-pasted request for bank information.
I was also, without my consent, nudged toward accepting the refund as a "coupon" via a "Fast Refund (Bonus)" option instead of the cash refund via bank transfer that I originally requested and confirmed.
A chargeback was apparently initiated on their end (2026-08-07) which I have never received clear written confirmation about.

I have a Klarna reference and a Case ID (2053808611884772) and a complete chat history documenting this entire pattern.

This is not a one-off mistake  it is a repeated, systemic pattern of stalling customers with scripted responses instead of resolving valid, confirmed refunds. €79.28 may not sound like much, but the way this has been handled  the same non-answer over and over for months  is completely unacceptable for a company of this size.

I would strongly caution anyone dealing with AliExpress customer service on a refund issue: document everything, because you will likely need it to escalate outside their own chat system (Klarna, consumer protection authorities, etc.), as their internal escalation process appears to not actually function.

After leaving a review on Trustpilot the seller finally decided to do a refund for 62usd from the 99usd purchase amount which is not bad even if it's not full amount and it's better than their initial offer of 30usd and the escalation team wasn't helpful either their responses seemed to be automated responses or BOT

data.review_body:
Refund Dispute – Order 8213871674453110

I am disputing the decision regarding order 8213871674453110, a 28-inch human hair wig that cost approximately $80. The wig arrived severely cut, with uneven lengths throughout and only one very small section reaching the advertised length. It was also poorly constructed, badly uneven, and had much lower density than advertised, making it completely unusable.
The item is advertised as a 28-inch product with a 200% density, which should weigh over 300 grams. However, after weighing the product myself, it only registers 180 grams. This is a severe shortage in weight and density compared to what was promised.
I submitted videos and extensive evidence clearly showing these defects and that the product was not as advertised. Despite this, the decision favored the seller, and I was offered only about $17, which is an extremely small amount compared with the $80 I paid for a defective and unusable product.

I believe a full refund or a fair devolution is justified. I would have preferred to return the product to the seller rather than receive such an inadequate refund. The seller should cover the return shipping costs for this unusable product and provide me with a full refund of the amount I paid.

UPDATE after Aliexpress reply my opinion here: Despite providing extensive evidence directly to AliExpress, including videos, photos, and proof of the wig’s weight and condition, my appeals have been rejected more than three times. I also uploaded additional videos showing the uneven cuts and the actual weight of the wig on YouTube and X/Twitter.

The product I received was significantly different from what was advertised, and I believe the evidence clearly demonstrates this. It is very disappointing that, despite providing multiple forms of evidence, AliExpress continues to consider them insufficient. I was a frequent AliExpress buyer, so this experience has been extremely disappointing. I am sharing this update so other buyers can make an informed decision.
SECOND UPDATE: still wating for a response

ATENCIÓN: ¡AliExpress YA NO es lo que era!

Leyendo otras reseñas, compruebo que mi caso no es un hecho aislado, sino la práctica fraudulenta habitual de esta empresa.

Mi caso particular: compré un mueble que tuve que devolver porque era defectuoso (auténtica basura, no te fíes de las fotos). Tras confirmar con el vendedor que, efectivamente, tenía una tara, pasé por una auténtica odisea para iniciar el proceso de devolución, que nunca llegó a buen puerto porque el propio vendedor rechazó el paquete. En cuanto vi el estado del envío, contacté con AliExpress para que me hicieran el reembolso y, después de varios chats surrealistas, me exigen que les envíe un justificante con sello y firma de la empresa de mensajería que indique el motivo de la no entrega. ¡Esto es algo que ningún transportista facilita y ellos lo saben perfectamente!

Por cierto, los GASTOS DE ENVÍO NO son GRATIS, como aseguran muchos de sus anuncios. ¡Hasta en esto engañan!

EDICTO: Responden a mi reseña, pero NO he recibido ninguna respuesta por parte de AliExpress en relación con la devolución de los gastos de envío.
data.review_headline: AliExpress no hace devoluciones ni reembolsa gastos de envío

data.review_body:
Vedr. ordrenr. 3075216798126431 som var et køb af en Android unit til min bil, virkede den ikke.
Jeg bad sælgeren, Podofo German Store om en retur adresse, samt email og et mobilnr.
Dette svarede han aldrig på, så jeg fandt en adr. på nettet i Frankfurt am Main, som jeg sendte pakken til, via UPS. 
Den blev nægtet modtaget og returneret til mig via UPS/Pakke.dk - det har koste mig 284,- kr. indtil videre plus selvfølgelig prisen på den uduelige Android unit, som kostede 143,16 euro = 1.080,- DKK.
Jeg har skrevet til sælgeren endnu engang og bedt om en korrekt returadresse, men han "spiller bare dum" og svarer ikke på det jeg beder om.
Det samme er tilfældet med AliExpress kundeservice, som ikke vil gå ind og bede sælgeren sende mig en returadresse - de "lukker sagen", fordi pakken ikke blev modtaget på fake adressen i Tyskland.
Når AliExpress sender mail til mig og skriver at de behandler sagen, på min email, kan man ikke besvare mailen fra dem. 
Sidste mail, med denne besked:
"We have conducted a thorough review regarding your request for this order. After careful consideration and verification, we regret to inform you that we are unable to proceed with a refund or compensation for this order.
We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this situation may cause and deeply appreciate your understanding and cooperation in this matter."

Det er så hvad man har ud af at handle med en platform, hvor sælgerne bare kan sende noget ubrugeligt bras og ikke vil modtage det retur.
data.review_headline: Vedr. en retursag, hvor jeg ikke kan returnere ubrugelig vare.

I never received my order. The delivery proof shows the parcel placed in mailbox #23105 — not mine. My mailbox is #23005, clearly different in number and color. The apartment linked to #23105 has no tenant, and I personally verified that mailbox is empty. The package is simply gone.

I opened a dispute with AliExpress and the seller, providing photo and video evidence of the mismatch, plus proof that the courier called me at delivery time but never actually handed over the parcel. My request was refused with no real investigation into the evidence I submitted — the case was closed as if the delivery photo alone settled it, ignoring that the mailbox in that photo belongs to no one.

I've spent over €1,000 on this platform over the past year and had further purchases planned. Instead of standing behind their own delivery partner's clear error, AliExpress closed my dispute and left me to absorb the loss of an order I paid for and never received.

If your delivery goes wrong here, don't expect AliExpress to actually look at your evidence before deciding against you.
Date of experience: 13/08/2026
Order number (optional): 3075636388397491 (également lié à 3075636388357491 et 3075636388417491, même envoi)

The automated mail you have sent is the 5 or 6 of its kind for my request and the appeal I have made, is the same as the one I got from your customer service.

Extremely disappointing experience with AliExpress Customer Service regarding Order #1115793412835663.

AliExpress officially verified and acknowledged the camera defect on my brand-new smartphone in writing ("indicated abnormality with phone camera function"). However, instead of issuing a refund or providing a prepaid return label, they are now using absurd stall tactics.

They have demanded an official inspection report from industrial cargo testing firms (BV, TUV, SGS, CCIC) within 48 hours for a single personal phone! This is an impossible requirement designed purely to deny legitimate buyer protection claims.

Written proof of defect exists on record.

Seller has no local repair center.

AliExpress refuses a fair refund or prepaid shipping label.

I am now escalating this matter to Tamara/Bank for a full Chargeback and submitting a regulatory complaint to econsumer.gov. 

Buyers beware: AliExpress "Buyer Protection" becomes a nightmare of impossible demands when a genuine hardware failure occurs.

data.review_body:
Update 27 August: still no email with a descent solution and still no parcel. 

Update: I received an email. Is this a joke? Again you ask us to take it up with DHL, but there is nothing to take up with DHL because the package is not there! This is disgraceful I have trying to get a solution sinds the beginning of August.

Terrible service — package never delivered, refund refused

Absolutely terrible experience. My package was never delivered to the stated home address. DHL confirmed that it was not delivered there and was also not available at the DHL depot

The situation became even more ridiculous: I was told the package could be collected from the depot and would then be relabelled. My friend went to collect it, only to be told that a QR code was required— a QR code that was never provided to us.

I contacted DHL directly, and they confirmed that the package was neither delivered to the address nor present at the depot.

Despite this, AliExpress keeps insisting that the package was delivered and refuses to issue a refund. Even worse, they refuse to properly investigate where the package actually went.

So basically: no package, no delivery, no investigation, and no refund.

This is completely unacceptable customer service. I strongly recommend thinking twice before ordering from this seller/platform. If something goes wrong with your delivery, don't expect them to take responsibility or actually investigate the problem.

Very disappointing and absolutely not the level of service you should expect when paying for a product you never receive.

data.review_body:
Intenté comprar una mesa anunciada por 172,24 €. La oferta indicaba claramente: IVA incluido, envío gratuito, ahorro en aranceles y sin cargos sorpresa adicionales en la entrega. Todo parecía perfectamente claro… hasta que llegó el momento de pagar.

Al acceder al checkout, el mismo producto, la misma variante, una sola unidad y la misma dirección de entrega pasaron mágicamente a costar 191,38 €. Aparecieron 19,14 € adicionales sin identificar, justificar ni desglosar.

Contacté con Atención al Cliente `por chat, envié las capturas y expliqué detalladamente lo sucedido. El propio agente revisó las pruebas, reconoció que se trataba de “un defecto del sistema” y escaló el caso para que pudieran arreglarlo.

¿La solución final de AliExpress? Una respuesta aparentemente automatizada indicándome que comprobara el carrito, que los impuestos podían recalcularse y que, si el precio no cumplía mis expectativas, buscara productos similares de otros vendedores.

La ironía es perfecta: AliExpress muestra un precio final, lo incrementa sin explicación al ir a pagar y su “solución” consiste en recomendar al cliente que compre otra cosa.

Un usuario necesita algo más que una respuesta automatizada. Una entidad como la suya debe ofrecer, además de respuestas absurdas como la facilitada, SOLUCIONES a los clientes.

Dispongo de una grabación completa de la pantalla que muestra todo el proceso, además de las capturas y la conversación en la que su propio agente reconoce el fallo. Por tanto, no se trata de una percepción ni de que el precio “no cumpla mis expectativas”: se trata de una diferencia objetiva entre el precio anunciado y el exigido en el checkout.

He solicitado que reabran el caso, expliquen y desglosen los 19,14 € añadidos y me permitan comprar el producto al precio anunciado, aplicando además el cupón disponible en ese momento.

Hasta que AliExpress ofrezca una solución real, mi experiencia puede resumirse así: un precio atractivo para llegar al checkout, un incremento inexplicable al pagar y un servicio de atención al cliente que responde sin analizar las pruebas.

Señores de AliExpress!!, dejen de hacer magia y nos tomen a los consumidores por tontos!!!
data.review_headline: 172 Precio todo incluido.  191€ al ir a pagar. La magia de AliExpress

Achat effectué en décembre 2025, matériel reçu le 7 juin 2026, moteur HS dès le 8 juin. Depuis, je tente sans succès d’obtenir une résolution amiable.

J’ai pourtant fourni tout ce qui pouvait l’être : environ 28 photographies, photos de la machine, de l’emballage et du moteur, vidéo montrant le dysfonctionnement, explications détaillées, échanges avec le vendeur et réponses aux e-mails d’AliExpress. La même vidéo a été transmise plusieurs fois.

Malgré cela, le service client me réclame régulièrement exactement les mêmes photos et la même vidéo, comme si le dossier repartait systématiquement de zéro. Conversations interrompues, nouveaux agents, nouvelles demandes, nouvelles explications, nouvelles escalades… puis retour au point de départ.

Je conserve l’ensemble des échanges et des preuves. Je ne suis évidemment pas responsable de la mauvaise conservation ou du mauvais suivi des pièces transmises par AliExpress.

Le plus aberrant est que le vendeur lui-même avait reconnu le problème et proposé l’envoi d’un moteur de remplacement. Cette solution impliquait toutefois 17,30 € de frais de livraison à ma charge, ce que j’ai refusé pour un produit tombé en panne dès le lendemain de sa réception.

AliExpress a malgré tout refusé de résoudre le problème. Trois escalades successives ont été effectuées auprès de leurs services supérieurs sans résultat concret.

Puis on m’a indiqué que mon dossier était clôturé parce que le délai pour agir aurait été dépassé, alors que ce sont précisément les multiples demandes de preuves, échanges et escalades d’AliExpress qui ont fait durer la procédure. Faire traîner un dossier puis reprocher au client le temps écoulé est particulièrement difficile à comprendre.

Et maintenant, nouvelle absurdité : on me demande des preuves concernant un écran tactile et un écran LCD.

Problème : la machine que j’ai reçue ne possède ni écran tactile ni écran LCD. Elle possède un affichage numérique à LED rouges et des commandes physiques.

Je ne peux donc pas fournir une vidéo démontrant une fonctionnalité qui n’existe pas sur le matériel reçu.

Si AliExpress considère que le produit concerné doit posséder un écran tactile et un écran LCD, alors pourquoi m’a-t-on livré un produit qui n’en possède aucun ?

On m’a également indiqué que certaines photographies fournies ne correspondaient pas à l’article acheté, alors que je signale justement cette incohérence concernant le matériel reçu.

Même l’application AliExpress a présenté des dysfonctionnements pendant la procédure : étapes affichées sans éléments interactifs, procédure disparaissant après avoir quitté et rouvert l’application, historique ne reflétant pas l’ensemble de mes démarches.

Et pendant tout ce temps, le problème initial n’a jamais changé :

le moteur est HS depuis le 8 juin 2026.

Le problème n’est donc plus simplement un produit défectueux : c’est l’incapacité du service après-vente à traiter correctement un dossier pourtant documenté.

Le client doit continuellement prouver qu’il a déjà prouvé.

Et après tout cela, la réponse publique d’AliExpress à mon avis Trustpilot consiste simplement à m’indiquer qu’un e-mail m’a été envoyé et que je dois le consulter.

Cette réponse ne répond à rien : ni à la panne, ni aux preuves transmises, ni aux demandes répétitives, ni aux incohérences concernant le produit, ni aux frais de livraison, ni à la clôture du dossier, ni aux mois de démarches.

Une réponse générique n’est pas une résolution.

Au 28 août 2026, soit plus de deux mois et demi après la panne, le moteur est toujours HS et aucune solution sérieuse n’a été apportée.

J’ai désormais conservé l’intégralité du dossier et je vais transmettre les éléments aux organismes compétents afin que cette affaire soit examinée en dehors du système AliExpress.

data.review_body:
Mes 2 premières commandes sur AliExpress, qui dépend du groupe chinois Alibaba, l’équivalent d’Amazon, ont conduit aux faits suivants :
1er produit, un disque dur externe de 1 TO : Le 1er disque dur envoyé buggait aux transferts de gros fichiers. Là, pas de problème, je peux renvoyer le disque dur défaillant, je suis remboursé et je recommande un autre disque dur d’une marque célèbre, TOSHIBA : plus de problème.
2ième produit, N° de référence: 3072425932562583, un ordinateur portable vendu par un commerçant français. Cet achat est destiné à changer mon ordinateur portable HP dont certaines touches commencent à être illisibles et avec un message de défaillance de la batterie. Lorsque j’ai du temps je décide de changer d’ordinateur. A l’ouverture de l’ordinateur reçu d’AliExpress je constate que c’est un clavier « qwerty » et non pas « azerty », donc gros problème pour moi dont mon usage d’un ordinateur portable est pour l’écriture car sur un clavier « qwerty » les lettres sont disposées autrement, mais surtout, il n’y a pas les accents sur les a, les e et les u, comme il n’y a pas le ç. J’explique dès mon 1er courriel du 9 mai le problème à AliExpress avec photographies des 2 claviers. Réponse d’AliEXpress : « Nous vous prions de bien vouloir fournir une preuve valide, sous forme de vidéo, démontrant que le produit reçu ne fonctionne pas correctement, et ce dans un délai de 24 heures. ». Je réponds que ce n’est pas un problème de fonctionneement (software) mais un problème de type de clavier. Et depuis les échanges s’enchaînent ; AliExpress reste sur le fonctionnement de l’ordinateur, et moi sur le problème matériel du clavier, fournissant des photographies et explications plus précises, y compris le rappel à la loi française, c’est-à-dire aux articles L217-4 à L217-7 du Code de la consommation. Et in fine, hier, je les informe que je vais leur faire de la publicité gratuite. Il faut enfin ajouter ce fait, le coût de ce produit : 303,92 €.

data.review_body:
Waardeloze garantie bij AliExpress: nul bescherming zodra een verkoper verdwijnt
​Koop op dit platform geen kostbare elektronica met de gedachte dat je garantie hebt. Ik heb een Junsun autoradio gekocht met een fabrieksgarantie van 2 jaar. Binnen deze garantietermijn begaf het apparaat het volledig. Om aan te tonen dat de inbouw en voeding in de auto 100% in orde waren, heb ik op eigen kosten een officieel rapport laten opstellen door een RDW-erkend autobedrijf. De diagnose was hard: een interne elektronische storing op de hoofdprintplaat van de radio.
​In de tussentijd is de winkel van de verkoper op AliExpress gesloten. Op dat moment zou de klantenservice van AliExpress het moeten overnemen en de garantie moeten waarborgen. De praktijk blijkt echter schrijnend:
​AliExpress biedt voor een product dat 100% defect is slechts een lachwekkende vergoeding van 30% aan.
​Nadat ik dit voorstel weigerde en verzocht om garantie (reparatie, vervanging, een volledige refund of store credit), weigert de klantenservice elke verdere medewerking omdat ik "het eerste bod heb afgewezen".
​Het platform neemt geen enkele verantwoordelijkheid voor verkopers die verdwijnen, terwijl ze wel commissie vangen over de verkopen.
​Kopersbescherming en 2 jaar garantie zijn bij AliExpress een lege belofte. Zodra een winkel de deuren sluit, verschuilt de klantenservice zich achter geautomatiseerde protocollen en laten ze de consument met een kapot product zitten. Wees gewaarschuwd!

I can buy these locally at $37 from Melbourne and I was looking for a grinder.  Picture matched, price was half the brand sells for so I took the plunge only to have a battery arrive!  I already have six so this duplicitous behaviour endorsing a vendor who is literally misrepresenting what he is selling, is very annoying.  Purchases BEWARE of what you purchase through this Chinese group.

Years as a customer and this is the first time I've needed help. Avoid.

The sellers either never responded or ignored the issues. The one with the fake postage even wanted me to order more things to "make things right". No thanks! That was my one and only experience with Aliexpress, I will not try them again. So my beef is with the terrible scammers they allow on their site, as in the end Aliexpress did come through and refund everything I ordered and never recieved.

premetto che cercavo una sella imbottita e rialzata per la mia moto, i prezzi anche su altre piattaforme a parità di "qualità" i prezzi di Aliexpress erano molto inferiori, Il pacco è arrivato nei tempi previsti ma purtroppo alla verifica dell'impiego l'oggetto non soddisfaceva le mie aspettative. Avviata la procedura di reso al momento in cui ho selezionato il corriere per la restituzione (BRT) il sistema invece di generare l'etichetta mi ha emesso un rimborso parziale di 15 euro (la sella costa 140!) allora ho cominciato a comunicare con il servizio clienti (molto probabilmente una IA ben fatta complimentosa ed accondiscendente) che ha aperto la contestazione e per bene 4 volte ha rifiutato il reso con rimborso perchè secndo la piattaforma avevo accettato tale rimborso parziale (??!!) per farla breve ho in casa una sella che non userò mai ho buttato via 130 euro! Quindi state alla larga da Aliexpres. Se potessi darei 0 stelle.
Aggiornamento del 20/08/2026 è arrivata la mail nel quale, come sempre la risposta "Siamo spiacenti di informarvi che la vostra richiesta di ricorso è stata
chiuso. Per quanto riguarda questa richiesta, abbiamo riveduto attentamente tutte le prove fornite, compresa la prova recentemente aggiornata, e abbiamo riscontrato che la prova non è sufficientemente efficace per supportare la tua affermazione." Ecco come volevasi dimostrare "non è sufficientemente efficace per supportare la tua affermazione." ma mi prendete per disonesto? Ho affermato allo sfinimento di aver richiesto il reso e rimborso il vostro sistema mi ha ingannato. Ditelo e basta non volete fare il reso ed ammettere che il vostro sistema non funziona. Ripeto state alla larga. Account cancellato e a chiunque mi chiederà di voi il giudizio sarà solo che negativo!
Aggiornamento numero 2: seconda mail del servizio clienti e mi ha detto che spedito una mail ribadendo il concetto che avevo accettato un rimborso parziale, quando invece avevo impostato una procedura di reso e rimborso completo! Ma questi sono fuori di testa!
Ultimo e definitivo aggiornamento: dopo la mail del servizio clienti e mia risposta, non si sono fatti più sentire. Come volevasi dimostrare! Ripeto STATE ALLA LARGA sono dei mangia soldi.

Ich bestellte im November 2025 zwei "Honor Original 100 W SuperCharge Ladestecker", die ich seit dem auch nutzte. Nun stellte ich fest, dass einer der beiden nicht mehr lädt. Ich testete mit einem anderen Kabel und einem anderen Gerät um sicher zu gehen, dass der Defekt am Ladestecker vorliegt. So war es dann auch. Nun gut, kann mal vorkommen. Glücklicher Weise befindet sich der Defekt noch weit in der Garantie/Gewährleistungsfrist! Schließlich lag der Kauf erst neun Monate zurück.
Ich reklamierte den Artikel also bei Aliexpress.
Hier verlangte man ein eindeutiges Video, welches den Defekt belegt. Ich sendete also ein Video, welches zeigt, das mein Smartphone beim Anschließen nicht reagiert!
Aliexpress verweigerte einen Ersatz bzw. eine Reparatur mit folgender Begründung: 

"Wir entschuldigen uns aufrichtig für Ihre Erfahrung und verstehen Ihre Bedenken. Leider können wir derzeit keine Rückerstattung veranlassen, da die vorgelegten Beweise kein qualitätsbedingtes Problem ausreichend belegen."

Mein Video zeigt eindeutig, das der Ladestecker ohne Funktion ist. Die drücken sich vor einer Rückerstattung...hier geht es um schlappe 13 Euro!?
Ich bin geheilt. Chinaware bleibt Chinaware!
Meine Einkäufe finden nicht mehr in Fernost statt, das ist sicher!
Beste Grüße

data.review_body:
purchased a bicycle battery and received an item that did not match the description. In practice, I received a product that is unusable for me.
When I contacted the seller, they avoided taking responsibility and did not provide a clear solution. I then escalated the issue through AliExpress.
The decision was that I should return the item, and the seller would refund both the cost of the product and the shipping expenses. However, the shipping costs had to be agreed upon in advance.
The problem is that in my country, batteries cannot be sent by regular post because they fall under the category of dangerous goods. I tried to agree with the seller on the costs of using private shipping companies, but the seller kept avoiding a direct answer as to whether they would cover those costs or not.
As a result, the time allocated for resolving the dispute expired, and AliExpress closed the case.
After that, I contacted customer support seven times, and every time the result was the same: an AI-generated email that completely ignored the problems described during the conversation.
My advice: use PayPal when paying for purchases on AliExpress. I have heard that PayPal handles such return cases in the customer’s favour much more quickly and easily.
To sum up, if a problem arises, you receive AI-based support that appears to be poorly trained, and in reality, you become trapped in a pointless exchange of messages. It seems designed to make you give up and forget about the platform.
data.review_headline: Very Poor Return and Dispute Resolution Experience

I ordered a Wi-Fi repeater for $38.88 (Order #1120394919272150). The device arrived completely dead—it will not turn on or broadcast any network.

I submitted clear video proof twice, showing the defect. AliExpress official dispute team responded with total nonsense: admitting the device is defective, but claiming "the goods still have certain value" to refuse a full refund! A completely dead piece of plastic has zero value.

To make matters worse, whenever I try to reach out on social media or support channels, I get hit with automated bot scripts and automated DMs across platforms. There is zero human customer service, zero accountability, and total ignorance of clear evidence.

They trap buyers with glitched bots and keep money for defective garbage. Avoid buying electronics here!


​Update: AliExpress replied with a generic template promising an email investigation, but order #1120394919272150 remains completely unresolved—this is just public PR damage control.
​To make matters worse, the seller tried to manipulate the system by offering a partial refund, but due to a technical glitch in AliExpress's own platform, the payout was never processed! Now, AliExpress falsely claims that the seller "already compensated" me, using their own system error as an excuse to deny a full refund for a completely dead device.
​Still no human response, zero actual compensation, and total support failure!

​Update: AliExpress is now using completely false transaction numbers to close this review!
​They claim Order #1120394919272150 was only $4.96. This is factually wrong. The total amount paid for this device was $38.88. $4.96 was merely a partial adjustment/coupon balance, NOT the cost of the item.
​Trying to publicize inaccurate, partial numbers to make it look like "case closed" is deceptive. I received a non-functional, completely dead Wi-Fi repeater, and AliExpress is still holding $33.92 of my money while claiming everything is resolved.
​Stop twisting transaction records for public PR. Issue the full $38.88 refund for the dead item!

​Update: AliExpress is attempting to mislead the public with false figures while ignoring direct evidence!
​According to my official invoice for Order #1120394919272150:
​Item Price: $55.38
​Bonus Balance Spent: $38.88 (earned funds, NOT discounts)
​Cash Paid: $4.96
​I have officially provided AliExpress with a clear video recording proving the PIX-LINK Powerline kit is completely dead and unusable.
​Despite clear video proof, they refuse to restore my $38.88 Bonus Balance, and their system currently shows only a paltry $1.00 cash refund issued!
​Denying full refunds and confiscating earned bonus balances on proven defective products is outright theft. Restore the $38.88 Bonus Balance and refund the full cash amount!

​Update: AliExpress is resorting to disgraceful stalling tactics and playing dumb!
​Ignoring Clear Video Proof: I provided an indisputable video showing the Wi-Fi repeater is completely dead. Yet, they keep claiming the evidence is "insufficient" just to tire me out and evade responsibility.
​Math Error & Bonus Credits Theft: I sent them the official payment breakdown proving the actual order value was $55.38, where $38.88 was paid using earned Bonus Balance and $4.96 in cash. They completely ignored this proof and falsely insisted the "total price" was only $4.96, issuing a insulting $1.00 partial refund!
​They are deliberately ignoring clear video evidence, refusing to correct their obvious calculation errors, and withholding earned bonus funds for a dead item. This is a deliberate attempt to wear me down. Stop playing games and issue the full refund immediately

​Update (Case Closed Fraudulently): AliExpress customer support has reached a new low.
​They officially emailed me claiming that I "confirmed and agreed" to a $1.00 partial refund on Order #1120394919272150. This is a complete lie. I never accepted any partial refund for a dead Wi-Fi kit, nor did I agree to forfeit my $38.88 in earned Bonus Credits. They are falsely closing disputes to avoid paying buyers back.
​To top it off, regarding Order #1121918957902150, they openly admitted they will not stop sellers from blacklisting buyers who report broken items.
​False claims of buyer agreement, stolen bonus balances, and complete protection for rogue sellers. Avoid AliExpress at all costs!
data.review_headline: Zero accountability: AliExpress sends defective electronics and hides behind bots!

Extremely disappointing experience with AliExpress and its customer service.

Order 3074763084437121. I returned a blue top that I had purchased through AliExpress, and the InPost tracking (820002887620010014839181) confirms that the parcel was shipped and received by the recipient.

AliExpress initially refused the refund and then claimed that “the item returned is different”, but has provided no clear evidence or explanation of what supposedly differs. The customer service is completely incapable of properly addressing the issue: instead of providing evidence or a concrete explanation, they simply repeat generic statements and close the appeal.

I have screenshots of the original order and of the item shown in my AliExpress app, as well as confirmation from InPost that the returned parcel was received. The original product page is no longer available.

At this point, I have neither the €105.69 I paid nor the returned item. This is an unacceptable way to handle a customer dispute. I have already escalated the matter through my bank and will take the matter further with the relevant authorities.

Very poor customer service and absolutely no meaningful explanation or resolution.

UPDATE 
After I posted my review, AliExpress finally sent me photos of what they claim was received. The item shown in the photos is a pair of shorts, not the blue top I returned.

Even more importantly, the photos show my name on the shipping label, but the packaging itself is NOT the package I sent. I returned the item in an H&M package. The package shown in AliExpress’ evidence is completely different.

I do not have a packing video because several weeks have passed since I returned the item, but I have witnesses who saw me put the correct item into the package and shipping it. The parcel was shipped on 1 August and, according to InPost tracking (820002887620010014839181), delivered on 14 August. (By the way, all this time??? And no one asks questions?? It should’ve been a couple of days, not weeks).

What is absolutely unacceptable is that AliExpress shows me evidence of a completely different package and item, yet does not seem interested at all in asking the courier what happened. If my label was attached to a different package, then obviously something happened during the return process — and somewhere there may be another customer who did not receive their own package either.

I did not choose the courier myself; the return shipping method was provided by AliExpress. Yet I am now expected to bear the entire financial loss for a problem that occurred after I handed the correct return to the courier.

I have already contacted InPost myself and requested an investigation, while AliExpress continues to focus only on the fact that I do not have a packing video instead of investigating the obvious discrepancy in the shipment.

I have neither my €105.69 nor the item I returned.

This is absolutely unacceptable and frankly disgraceful customer service. I expect AliExpress to investigate what happened to my parcel with the courier instead of simply refusing my refund.

UPDATE 6: I sent the supplier pics of the cables cut up to be put in trash, and a professional test of the cables which said "the USB-C CC connection/resistor is missing or incorrectly fitted, you should return or request refund". The supplier is now offers a limited refund - BUT "due to their policy it cant be processed until late November", (3 months time!), and I would have to contact them again. I have only continued with this nonsense to find out how far they would take it and now I know - they will do anything rather than refund you. I've told them to poke it and their refund.
UPDATE 5: So after yet another review, sent more images, videos, they have concluded “insufficient evidence of faulty goods” LOL. How can you send evidence that a cable doesn’t work, other than showing it plugged in and not working, while another one does. AliEx are determined not to refund or replace, so will clearly continue to sell faulty and substandard goods to customers. Their approach is to promise free returns and cheap prices but don’t mention shoddy products and NO customer service. UPDATE 4: Now being asked to complete a satisfaction survey! So I tried, but it’s all in Russian....!!! 
UPDATE 3: The seller has offered a 10% discount on USB cables, all of which are useless and will not connect or charge my phone and so will have to go in the trash. I have also sent them all the information and photo proof. They just increased the offer to 20% which amounts to less than a 1£ UK per cable, and is useless as the cables are junk. I asked for replacements that work, and they stated that they do not offer replacements (for faulty goods).
AliExpress have now closed this complaint and said it is completed. There is only one conclusion to be drawn, and that is never ever by anything from AliExpress if you are not prepared to lose all your money and not get what you paid for.
UPDATE 2: another response from AliExpress again asking me to send an unboxing video of 3USB cables and proof that they don't work. Have already sent countless photographs of them plugged in and not working next to one that does. I've given up now, as it's obvious that they are not intending to deal fairly with the issue and just keep finding new excuses. Plus asking me to complate a 60 item questionnaire for an item under £5......... 

 Untrustworthy total fraud of a website. Have bought countless items from eBay and Temu. Occasionally there’s a problem and always it’s been dealt with professionally and in a fair way. AliExpress is totally different. Ordered 3 USB C cables, and none of them worked, none would charge my iPhone or iPad. Agreed to return for a credit, but just got the clearly deliberate runaround. As requested I sent them a photo of my own cable charging my phone showing  the green charging light, and another of my phone plugged into the same USB port with one of the cables they sent me, and no connection at all. AliExpress came back and said it wasn’t sufficient evidence, so I sent them two more photographs showing the full length for the cables and the exact same usb port they were plugged into and how they didn’t work. They came back and said they’d closed the review due to insufficient evidence. It is then impossible to proceed further as they just put up barrier after barrier of nonsense, like have you read the manual? data.review_body:
## ⭐ Buyer Protection That Doesn't Protect

I wanted to trust AliExpress, but my recent experience has completely changed my opinion.

## 📦 Damaged Items on Arrival

I received:

* **Solar eclipse glasses** with the filter lens folded and creased (a serious safety concern).
* **A vinyl car sticker** that was bent and wrinkled because it wasn't shipped flat.

Both items were clearly damaged during shipping due to poor packaging.

## 📷 I Provided Plenty of Evidence

I submitted:

* Multiple clear photos
* Close-up images
* Different angles
* Additional evidence every time it was requested

Despite this, AliExpress kept responding that my evidence was "not sufficient" and asked for even more.

## 🤷 Endless Requests, No Resolution

It felt like the goal wasn't to investigate the issue—it was simply to keep asking for more evidence until the buyer gave up.

When an item is obviously defective, buyers shouldn't have to repeatedly prove the same thing.

## ❌ Buyer Protection Felt Meaningless

The buyer protection policy sounds reassuring, but in my experience it didn't provide any real protection.

If damaged items with clear photographic evidence still don't qualify for a straightforward refund, I have to question how effective the dispute system really is.

## ⚠️ My Advice

Be cautious when buying from AliExpress.

If something arrives damaged, don't assume the buyer protection policy will work as advertised. My experience has left me with very little confidence in the platform, and I will think twice before ordering from them again.
data.review_headline: DEFECTIVE ITEM - NOT SUPPORTIVE NOT HELPFUL

Tanto AliExpress como PayPal engañan a sus clientes con descuentos que luego no ofrecen. Compre una estación de energía Oukitel P2100E Plus con descuentos por 442€. Ofrecían un descuento adicional de 33€ por un importe superior a 299€ si realizabas el pago mediante PayPal. Pues bien, tras la compra no recibí ese descuento y al reclamar a AliExpress se lavaron las manos alegando que esa promoción ya habia caducado. Acto seguido cancele la compra. Visite de nuevo la tienda y sorpresa, la promoción seguía activa. Les recuerdo a estos sinverguenzas que es ilegal ofrecer descuentos si luego no se aplican y espero que esta denuncia sirva para desenmascarar a estos sinverguenzas. data.review_body:
​Title:Deceptive Checkout System & Predatory Shipping Charges — Case Ref:3075642513206header
​AliExpress and the seller "Gather Here Store" are engaging in predatory & deceptive sales practices.
​I attempted to purchase 3 small wooden stamps from the same store in a single transaction. However, their broken system enforced an arbitrary purchasing limit of "1 unit per order", physically forcing me to split my purchase into multiple separate transactions. As a direct result, I was charged duplicate shipping fees (£2.66 each time)—a complete rip-off engineered by a system flaw.
​To make matters worse, the listings repeatedly claim "only 1 left in stock" to induce panic buying, yet the stock magically replenishes immediately after payment.
​When I raised this with customer service, an agent named Umar falsely assured me before checkout that the issue was resolved. It was not. The so-called "higher-level escalation" resulted in nothing more than a generic, copy-pasted email ignoring the actual technical glitch & refusing to refund the overcharged delivery fees.
​I have paid over £41 for these items—a subtotal that easily exceeds their £28 free-shipping threshold—yet I was scammed into paying duplicate shipping due to their system's refusal to combine orders.
​I demand an immediate refund of the £5.32 overcharged shipping fee and an investigation into this fake scarcity tactic. I have full screenshot evidence of every chat log, system error, and invoice, and I will report this to the UK Financial Ombudsman and Consumer Rights authorities if left unresolved.
Ms Ho

Updated Review on 19 August 2026
Title: A £300 Deceptive Trap - How AliExpress Exploits "Fairness" for Profit
​Review:
I am writing this to expose how AliExpress and its sellers (specifically Gather Here Store) manipulate the system to exploit buyers. I attempted to purchase a 15-piece wooden stamp set. Individually, these items are priced around £20 each. For a full set, this represents a significant investment of approximately £300.
​The "Fairness" Scam:
The seller intentionally broke the 15-piece set into 15 separate listings. AliExpress then imposed a strict limit of "1 item per order." To acquire the full set, I was forced to place 15 separate orders. Because they split the listings, I was forced to pay £2.66 in shipping for every single item—totalling nearly £40 in unnecessary shipping fees.
​When I challenged this, AliExpress customer support claimed these limits were set by the seller to ensure "fair buying opportunities for everyone" during a promotion. This is a blatant, insulting lie:
​They are selling wooden stamps, not scarce medical supplies or emergency goods. There is zero logical reason to enforce "anti-hoarding" rules on stationery.
​The system allows me to buy all 15 pieces, but only if I pay the seller 15 separate shipping fees. Where is the "fairness" in paying 15x the shipping cost for a single transaction?
​This is purely a deceptive tactic to bypass "Free Shipping" thresholds and extract hidden profits from customers.
​AliExpress support has proven useless, repeatedly stalling with requests for "supplementary documents" every 48 hours to delay resolution. They essentially told me to negotiate shipping fees directly with the seller. If I have to deal with the seller directly to resolve platform traps, then the AliExpress platform serves no purpose other than to facilitate these scams.
​Be warned: This platform is not a marketplace; it is a trap designed to extract extra fees through absurd, artificial restrictions. Do not trust their "promotions" or "fairness" claims.

Updated on 20 August 2026

​If you are planning to buy any electronics or items with a warranty on AliExpress, think twice. My experience with their customer care and seller warranty support has been an absolute nightmare and a masterclass in dodging responsibility.
​I purchased a fitness tracker (Order #1118274496035281) which worked fine for six months before completely dying overnight. It won’t charge, it won’t turn on, and it’s completely unresponsive. The seller confirmed in writing that the product has a one-year warranty.
​When I tried to claim it, I was dragged through weeks of automated bot loops. After finally reaching a human support agent, their response was infuriatingly absurd: they claimed that the video I provided “failed to detect the defect of the equipment” and demanded a video showing the “obvious defects when you use the equipment.”
​How on earth are you supposed to "use" a device that is completely dead and won't charge?! What do they expect? A magic show?
​This is a deliberate, transparent tactic to exhaust customers and cheat them out of valid warranty claims. They hide behind impossible demands ("official inspection reports" or videos of a dead brick performing functions) so they never have to honor a single refund or replacement.
​AliExpress Customer Care does not care about consumers. Save your money, buy from reputable local retailers, and avoid getting scammed by their fake "warranties."


Stop playing PR games. Your public reply here is completely fake and just for show.
​Right after posting this nice public apology, your support team sent me an email demanding that I provide a "valid quality inspection report issued by a third-party company like BV, TUV, SGS, or CCIC" for a six-month-old fitness tracker!
​Are you out of your minds? Do you seriously expect a regular consumer to hire an international industrial testing laboratory and pay hundreds of dollars to inspect a cheap consumer electronics item just to honor a basic warranty?
​This is not a "process"—it is a deliberate, absurd scam designed to make warranty claims impossible. You hide behind bureaucratic jokes so you never have to refund or replace a single broken product.
​Future buyers, take warning: AliExpress "warranties" are entirely worthless. Do not buy electronics here.

⭐ 1 Stern – Sehr enttäuschende Erfahrung mit dem Kundenservice

Ich habe bei AliExpress Echthaar für über 200 € bestellt. Leider entsprach die Qualität nach kurzer Zeit nicht mehr meinen Erwartungen: Das Haar wurde stumpf, verfilzte bzw. verhedderte sich, die Dichte nahm in den Längen deutlich ab und die Enden waren teilweise extrem dünn und wirkten abgebrochen.

Ich habe zunächst versucht, das Problem direkt mit dem Verkäufer zu lösen. Der Verkäufer machte mir im Laufe der Kommunikation mehrere unterschiedliche Angebote zur Rückerstattung. Ich war sogar bereit, dem Verkäufer noch eine weitere Chance zu geben und erneut bei ihm zu bestellen, da ich davon ausgehe, dass möglicherweise eine schlechte Charge die Ursache gewesen sein könnte.

Da wir keine endgültige Lösung fanden, wandte ich mich an den AliExpress-Kundenservice.

AliExpress forderte ausdrücklich Video-/Bildbeweise. Ich habe daraufhin ZWEI Videos eingereicht, in denen das Haar selbst der klare Fokus ist. Das Haar wurde aus mehreren Perspektiven, aus der Nähe und in verschiedenen Bereichen gezeigt, damit die Qualität, die Struktur, die Dichte und insbesondere die sehr dünnen und beschädigten wirkenden Enden deutlich erkennbar sind.

Zunächst wurde mir mitgeteilt, es seien keine Beweise vorgelegt worden. Nachdem ich darauf hingewiesen hatte, dass ich zwei Videos eingereicht habe, änderte sich die Begründung: Nun hieß es, die Beweise seien zwar vorhanden, würden aber nicht ausreichen. Eine konkrete Erklärung, welcher Teil der Videos nicht erkennbar sein soll, erhielt ich nicht.

Anschließend wurde plötzlich ein Qualitätsbericht eines Drittanbieters verlangt.

Ich habe mehrfach ausführlich erklärt, dass es sich um einen sichtbaren Qualitätsmangel des Produktes handelt und dass das Produkt selbst in den Videos eindeutig zu sehen ist. Trotzdem erhielt ich wiederholt nahezu wortgleiche Standardantworten.

Was mich besonders enttäuscht, ist nicht nur die Ablehnung meiner Rückerstattung, sondern dass ich das Gefühl hatte, dass meine konkreten Beweise und meine ausführliche Erklärung überhaupt nicht individuell geprüft wurden. Ich habe immer wieder dieselben Antworten erhalten, ohne eine konkrete Auseinandersetzung mit meinen Videos oder dem Chatverlauf mit dem Verkäufer.

Bei einem Warenwert von über 200 € hätte ich eine ernsthafte und nachvollziehbare Prüfung erwartet.

Ich habe dem Verkäufer und auch AliExpress mehrfach die Möglichkeit gegeben, eine faire Lösung zu finden. Leider hatte ich am Ende den Eindruck, dass so lange Standardantworten wiederholt wurden, bis der Kunde irgendwann aufgibt.

Für mich ist das eine sehr enttäuschende Erfahrung. Nicht wegen einer einzelnen schlechten Lieferung, sondern vor allem wegen des Umgangs mit meiner Reklamation und der fehlenden nachvollziehbaren Begründung für die Ablehnung.

Ich kann aufgrund dieser Erfahrung aktuell leider keine positive Empfehlung für den AliExpress-Kundenservice aussprechen.


Nachtrag: Nachdem ich diese Bewertung abgegeben habe, kontaktiert mich der Kundenservice erneut. Auch hier war ich voller Hoffnung und kooperativ.  Ich habe nicht nur 2 Videos für die Beweise der Qualität vorgelegt,  sowie mehrere Fotos.  Auch hier bekam ich daraufhin wieder die gleiche Standard-Antworten.  Es ist wirklich unglaublich,  zusätzlich sperrte mich der Verkäufer, der eine letzte sehr arrogante Nachricht zusandte..ich bin fassungslos.  Gerne korrigiere ich diese Bewertung , falls ich mich einigen kann.

data.review_body:
AliExpress account stuck in an endless authentication loop for over two months. Password reset works for three days, then the system forces another reset. On iPhone I cannot log in at all.
Case ID: 2053808358289979
Dozens of support tickets, only automated replies. No human has reviewed this case. Requesting escalation to a technical engineer.

UPDATE 19/08: I regained access on 18/08 via password reset on desktop, and password is currently the only working sign-in method. During testing, password, email code, passkey and Google all led to a forced "Change password" screen. Passkey authentication completed successfully but then returned "Account disabled", and the "Enable Now" button on that screen links to survey.aliexpress.com — a closed page. There is no working self-service recovery path. The recovery URL contained identityScene=RELEASE_STOLEN, which suggests a security flag remains on the account.

UPDATE 23/08: Still no response since my reply of 19 August, and the 7–14 business day window AliExpress stated has now passed. Desktop sign-in with password has been stable for two weeks, but passkey sign-in still returns "Account disabled" and the "Enable Now" button still redirects to a closed survey page. I have not reinstalled the app on my iPhone, because every previous attempt triggered an "unusual activity" lock that also broke my working desktop session — and AliExpress has not answered my request for guidance on how to safely sign in from that device. On 19/08 AliExpress invited me to reply to their agent directly. When I did, the same mailbox returned an automated message stating that emails sent to it are not received. There is now no working channel through which this case can be reached.

UPDATE 26/08 — FINAL: Desktop access has now been lost as well. After two weeks of stable sign-in, I am locked out of every device. Three months, dozens of tickets, and this is where it ends.

The record speaks for itself. AliExpress told me the problem was fixed — it was not, and I proved it with screenshots the same day. They asked me questions, I answered in full, and they never replied. They invited me to write to their agent directly, and that same mailbox now auto-replies that emails to it are not received. Their own "Enable Now" recovery button leads to a dead survey page. There is not one working channel left through which a customer can reach a human being about a broken account.

This is not a technical failure. A technical failure gets fixed. This is a company that has decided that individual customers are not worth answering — that a buyer of many years can be locked out of his own account for three months, document everything, follow every instruction given to him, and simply be ignored until he gives up. That is the actual policy, whatever the support templates say.

To anyone reading this before you buy: the products may be cheap, but if anything goes wrong with your account there is no one behind the counter. Not a person, not a phone number, not a working email. You are entirely on your own.

I am done. Case ID: 2053808358289979 — unresolved, abandoned.

data.review_body:
This serves to denounce yet another of the thousands of frauds perpetrated by AliExpress.

There is an advertisement published on AliExpress, already reported by me, for an item that does not exist but is still for sale. 
The situation is as follows: the customer is deceived, makes the purchase because the information states that there are 96 available, but in reality, none exist. If payment is made by credit card, then they lose the money. If payment is made with PayPal, then they receive an item that has nothing to do with the original, and which they will later complain about, but the store simply does not respond and then ceases to exist. In other words, basically you either lose your money or you get an item that has nothing to do with what was advertised.

This store and the ad were reported to AliExpress, who replied that they would penalize the seller, which turned out to be yet another complete scam. They remain active and continue to deceive customers. A clear fraud, reported but completely ignored by AliExpress, which is equally fraudulent in contributing to these situations happening.
aliexpress. item/1005012891096164.

Here's what happened: this seller tried to sell me this item, which I later realized, due to my extensive experience with this type of fraud, could be an attempted scam.

I questioned the seller about the actual availability of the item and its true correspondence with the original item; note that he stated there were 96 scooters of that model available.

After investigating this seller further, I found that there were defrauded customers who received scooters that were not the ones advertised and were never able to return them, something that has happened to me several times with Aliexpress – another complete fraud.

Add to this the fact that the seller suggested another scooter because this one didn't actually exist; that is, the advertised scooter doesn't exist, and this fact is evident in the messages exchanged with the seller and already sent as proof to Aliexpress.

Now it's just a matter of verifying the facts:

1. Offering an item (electric scooter) for sale that does not exist - attempting to sell a non-existent item constitutes fraud/attempted scam.

2. Providing a number of 96 available items when in fact that item does not exist - Misleading information to the customer/is a crime of fraud.

Now it's easy to understand: Aliexpress has an advertisement from a seller who is not only deceiving customers but continues to perpetrate this crime with impunity, with the complicity of Aliexpress, despite the evidence and confirmation that the scooter does not exist. Therefore, there is nothing more to understand here.

NOTE: THIS RESPONSE FROM ALIEXPRESS, AS WE KNOW, IS JUST ANOTHER SCAM FROM THIS PLATFORM, WHICH ACTS UNIQUELY LIKE A TRUE GANG OF CRIMINALS.

19/08/2026 
These responses from AliExpress are all lies. They did absolutely nothing. There is a fraud, of which I presented proof, deceiving customers, and they collaborate with all of this. Simply a bunch of criminals.

I bought a baby monitor. The item was slow to be delivered. When it finally arrived, it came with the wrong charging cord, so I couldn’t even charge the screen. When I contacted the seller, they refused to simply send a replacement cord and instead wanted me to return the entire item.

Rather than wait weeks for it to be returned, processed, refunded and then repurchase the monitor, I bought a compatible cord myself so I could actually use the baby monitor.

After only a few days of use, I noticed severe LCD light bleed around the screen. I contacted the seller again to request a replacement screen. What followed was hours of back-and-forth. At one point, I agreed to a partial refund, only to then be told that they actually couldn’t offer it.

I was ultimately told I would need to send the entire item back, wait for it to arrive, and then they would decide whether I was entitled to a refund.

For a product that arrived with the wrong cord and then developed a significant screen defect within days, this has been an incredibly frustrating experience.

BUYER BEWARE!


EDIT:
AliExpress responded to my review saying they had sent me an email. They did — but the email simply repeated the same response I had already received: send the entire order back for assessment before they will consider a refund. No actual assistance or resolution was offered. Just another obstacle to getting a working monitor. Shame.

“Alerta: recibí un producto completamente diferente al comprado — Guía ML623358526MH”
Reseña:
Título: Incumplimiento en pedido — Guía ML623358526MH

Incumplimiento en pedido — Guía ML623358526MH

Bajo la guía ML623358526MH compré una tablet Lenovo de 11". Sin embargo, recibí un paquete cuyo contenido correspondía a piezas de plástico y cartón, y no al producto adquirido.

Presenté como evidencia un video continuo del proceso de desempaque, fotografías de la guía de transporte, medidas físicas del paquete y documentación relacionada con el pedido. También aporté información sobre las dimensiones del envío, como elemento adicional para demostrar que el contenido recibido no correspondía con el producto comprado.

A pesar de las pruebas presentadas, la reclamación fue cerrada desfavorablemente y no obtuve el reembolso correspondiente.

El aspecto que considero más preocupante de esta experiencia no es únicamente haber recibido un producto diferente al adquirido, sino el resultado del proceso posterior de reclamación. Cuando un comprador presenta documentación, fotografías, medidas y un video continuo del desempaque, espera que dichas pruebas sean evaluadas de manera objetiva y que exista un mecanismo efectivo para resolver el incumplimiento.

En este caso, el resultado ha generado una pérdida de confianza tanto en la protección ofrecida al comprador como en el procedimiento utilizado para evaluar las evidencias dentro de la plataforma.

Por esta razón, después de esta experiencia no considero que pueda recomendar la plataforma con la misma confianza que tendría antes de realizar la compra. La decisión final de continuar utilizándola corresponde a cada comprador, pero considero importante que otros usuarios conozcan lo ocurrido y tengan presente que la existencia de un mecanismo interno de reclamación no garantiza que una controversia sea resuelta favorablemente, incluso cuando el comprador presenta evidencias que considera relevantes.

Ante una situación similar, resulta importante conservar desde el inicio la publicación original, comprobantes de pago, información del pedido, número de guía, fotografías del paquete, sus dimensiones y un registro continuo del desempaque. Si la reclamación interna no resulta favorable, también puede ser conveniente consultar con la entidad financiera que procesó el pago qué mecanismos de disputa están disponibles de acuerdo con las condiciones aplicables a la tarjeta y a la transacción.
AliExpress actúa como intermediario en la operación y dispone de un sistema de Protección al Comprador para resolver controversias. Sin embargo, en mi experiencia, el proceso de reclamación presentó deficiencias importantes. La decisión adoptada no consideró adecuadamente, a mi juicio, las pruebas físicas y métricas aportadas, entre ellas el video de desempaque y las dimensiones del paquete recibido. Además, algunos de los requisitos probatorios solicitados resultaron difíciles de obtener dentro de los plazos establecidos. Esta experiencia plantea dudas sobre la eficacia del sistema de Protección al Comprador frente a casos en los que existe una discrepancia entre el producto adquirido y el contenido físicamente recibido.
Esta reseña se basa en mi experiencia concreta con el pedido identificado mediante la guía ML623358526MH y en el proceso de reclamación realizado posteriormente.
data.review_headline: Alerta: recibí un producto completamente diferente al comprado — Guía ML623358526MH”

data.review_body:
Je suis extrêmement déçue par AliExpress et, pour la première fois, par son service client.

J’ai commandé sur AliExpress un produit d’une valeur de 131 €, que j’attendais depuis longtemps et dont j’avais réellement besoin pour mon enfant en situation de handicap.

D’après les informations de livraison, le livreur aurait simplement déposé mon colis au rez-de-chaussée de mon immeuble, pris une photo comme preuve de livraison, puis serait parti. Or, j’habite au dernier étage. Personne ne m’a appelée, je n’ai reçu aucun SMS et personne ne m’a prévenue que mon colis avait été laissé sans surveillance dans une partie commune de l’immeuble.

Je ne sais donc pas ce qui s’est passé ensuite. Le colis a-t-il été repris par le livreur ? A-t-il été pris par quelqu’un d’autre ? Je ne peux accuser personne sans preuve. Mais une chose est certaine : je n’ai jamais reçu ce colis et je ne l’ai jamais eu entre les mains.

Cela fait maintenant deux semaines que j’essaie d’obtenir de l’aide. Le service client d’AliExpress me répond toujours pratiquement la même chose, sans apporter de véritable solution. Mon remboursement a été refusé, mon colis reste introuvable et mes 131 € ont disparu avec lui.

AliExpress choisit ses partenaires de livraison et travaille avec eux. En tant que cliente, je considère donc qu’AliExpress doit également assumer sa responsabilité lorsqu’une livraison se passe mal et intervenir réellement auprès du transporteur pour comprendre ce qui s’est passé, au lieu de laisser le client seul face au problème.

Je trouve particulièrement choquant qu’une simple photo d’un colis posé dans les parties communes d’un immeuble puisse être considérée comme une preuve suffisante de livraison au destinataire. Une photo d’un colis abandonné au rez-de-chaussée ne prouve absolument pas que le client l’a reçu.

Après toutes ces années à commander sur AliExpress, je n’aurais jamais imaginé me retrouver dans une telle situation. Je suis profondément déçue par la manière dont mon dossier est traité.

Aujourd’hui, je me retrouve sans mon produit et sans mes 131 €.

Après cette expérience, je ne souhaite malheureusement plus commander sur AliExpress et je ne peux pas recommander ce site à mon entourage. Il existe d’autres plateformes qui prennent davantage leurs responsabilités lorsqu’un colis n’arrive pas réellement entre les mains du client.

J’espère malgré tout qu’AliExpress finira par examiner sérieusement mon dossier, identifier le transporteur et le livreur concernés, et me proposer enfin une solution juste : retrouver mon colis ou me rembourser intégralement les 131 €.

data.review_body:
⭐ 1 Star — Appalling Customer Service & Invasive Verification Process
I have been an AliExpress customer since 2012 — over 13 years — with successful orders shipped to the UK and Austria. When I attempted to place a simple 77 EUR order to Vietnam where I am currently travelling, my payment was repeatedly declined with error code CSC_7200026 (risk scanning — NOT a timeout as their agents kept incorrectly insisting).

What followed was 3+ days of the most frustrating customer service experience I have ever encountered:
❌ Multiple agents sending identical copy and paste responses about a “payment timeout” that had nothing to do with my actual issue

❌ Being escalated to a “higher team” who sent the exact same generic email

❌ Being asked to submit my PASSPORT, a photo of my PHYSICAL BANK CARD including full card number, AND a BANK STATEMENT — for a 77 EUR purchase

❌ Not a single agent actually reading or addressing my specific situation
The verification process they demand is frankly indistinguishable from what identity fraudsters request. No legitimate company should ask a verified 13 year customer to hand over this level of sensitive personal documentation for a low value order. I refused and I stand by that decision.


The irony? I eventually resolved the issue myself by creating a new account in incognito mode. AliExpress’s own customer service team could not resolve in 3 days what took me 10 minutes to fix independently.


The platform works when it works. But their customer service is automated, impersonal and completely unfit for purpose. If you ever encounter a payment issue — good luck. You’re on your own.
Would not recommend relying on their support team for anything.

De verkoper probeert me bovendien op te lichten door te vragen het geschil te sluiten. Ik pik dit niet langer. Ik eis dat een manager per direct handmatig de status omzet naar 'Refund Only'. Mijn bank ing is inmiddels ook op de hoogte gesteld van deze iDEAL-wanprestatie.
u
update: the arbitration team ignored all evidence. They are forcing me via an automated message to return a dangerous  
lithium battery   this is illegal and rejected by  post nl.
This is consumer deception
I demand that the ebcare team changes this case to refund only immediately order 3075325794689654
.UPDATE MAANDAG: AliExpress blijft consumenten misleiden. Ze sturen vandaag een e-mail waarin ze eisen dat ik zelf de verzendkosten voorschiet naar Duitsland en dat ik slechts een tegoedbon terugkrijg voor de verzending. Update 27/8/26  AliExpress seller Asometech As you can see from the above I had provided 2 videos, now I have provided 4 each one with additional information, all rejected with the comment failed to demonstrate the quality issue. Lets be clear the issue with this device is it is dead, does not turn on.It only has one switch so there is no confusion. There is only one way you can demonstrate this is issue is to plug the power lead into a mains socket and then into the back of the charger, how else could you demonstrate the issue. It is evident that this is what they do, reply to your video with a standard email until you give up. They are a disgraceful organization and especially this seller Asometech. data.review_body:
On April 27, 2026, I ordered a car multimedia system for $52.06, including shipping. The package was held up at customs. Customs required an invoice on my name, specifying the exact name and technical specifications of the multimedia system, in order to release the package. I contacted the seller twice to request these documents, but the seller failed to provide them. I attempted to clear the package through customs myself but was unsuccessful without the required documentation. After 45 days, as the necessary documents had not been received, the package was sent for destruction. I opened a dispute, providing evidence that the seller had failed to supply the documents needed for customs clearance, resulting in the failed release. The dispute was closed without any explanation. I appealed the decision to close the dispute and submitted further proof of the seller's failure to provide the documents; however, the appeal was also closed without a logical explanation. I repeatedly appealed the decision to close the dispute, yet I received only dozens of automated, copy-paste responses. Very poor and disappointing service for a long-time customer with thousands of purchases. I do not recommend buying there; it is better to switch to other sites like eBay, Amazon, or Temu.

After my review here and contacting AliExpress on Instagram, I received a message that my appeal was being reviewed.
I received a positive decision on my appeal with all the evidence.

data.review_body:
I bought something from AliExpress, a motherboard that was meant to arrive by August 6th. It didn't arrive, and I found out I had to pay for customs, which I was okay with. I understand that. But then AliExpress said my parcel would arrive after I paid. I got an email saying it would arrive by August 10th. I waited, but no parcel arrived. I looked at my tracking, and it said it had been delivered. How could it have been delivered if no one knocked on my door? I searched for the parcel, but it was nowhere to be found. Then I looked again, and it said it had been picked up from a pick-up point two days ago, after I paid the tax online. So, I literally paid for someone to get my parcel and have it for themselves.

I contacted AliExpress many times, and I contacted the store that sold it many times. They told me to contact the seller, then told me to contact AliExpress customer service, who told me to contact PostNL, who wouldn't help. So, I contacted AliExpress again many times to request a refund. They won't give me a refund for it as they don't have evidence, all because their website says it's delivered, but it's clearly not delivered. I wouldn't be here wasting my time going through this to get my 244 pounds, plus what I paid for customs, which was 51 pounds, which is ridiculous. So, I have been scammed out of 295 pounds.

Now the store doesn't even reply to me. AliExpress keeps canceling my refund. I already know I can't get the Declaration of Non-Receipt from PostNL because they keep saying it's delivered, which clearly hasn't been delivered. They are so useless, as is AliExpress. It's like they are doing this together. AliExpress bots are even worse; it takes forever to talk to a human. I can't believe this. I thought this was a genuine place to buy a motherboard.

Habe bereits mehrere Handys, Handyhüllen, Lego, Backutensilien, Kleider, Katzenspielzeug, Nintendo Switsch Controller und und und und.... bestellt. Höchst selten das etwas nicht gut war. Kanns geben aber bitte leute, schaut euch die Bewertung vom Shop an!!! Das günstigste ist nicht immer das gleiche wie der Offizielle Store wo das gleiche 10% mehr kostet, also den fehler macht bitte nur einmal. Was viele nicht checken: das ist ein Marktplatz kein Geschäft! Viele Div Händler die im Kundschaft werben. 
Wenn mal was Defekt war, habe ich fotos gemacht geschickt und ohne Diskusion Geld zurück bekommen oder ersatz wurde geliefert! Stern abzug weil man halt wirklich die Spreu vom Weizen trennen muss. Das muss man selber machen, dafür bekommt ihr da das gleiche Produkt wie hier für nen Bruchteil der Kosten! Und bitte hört auf mit dem Kostenlosen versand-Filter! 
So und nun viel spass beim Shoppen!

The issue with Aliexpress & Alibaba is in essence that they scam the market. 
When requesting more info and a final quote from sellers - prices on the products has more than doubled ... transport costs are hilarious and you have no backing - no support, when things goes south. As such - the best advise I can give to people trying to do business on those scam services.... is DON´t 
That is unless you want to waste your life being fooled by red China.

16.08 update 

I tried to react to their feedback - but somehow it would not go through. As such I would like to clarify that when I on EBAY buys merchandise at a given price, with pictures showing the item - and I order it ... I get it as described. 
When EBAY is offering me selections - the price adjust - and there is no doubt that with the adjustment and a new price ... I now have a new fixed real price... 
When I work with the ALI´es of this world... its not the shown item that I am buying ...  even choosing the options .. it is scam to lour me into a product thatmost likely is the same ....  but now 3 times more expensive. All the so called discounts - and bl.a bl.a after hitting the buy button .. its just SCAM ... Whe I buy it on Etsy, Ebay and more ... I know what I am getting.... I bought a generator, a lift and a greenhouse   ....fake it was, all of it. Ended up asking my money back... so giving my money to ALI for them to handle my money and make money on that I am just a fool ...  waiting for my money to come back. It´s a disgrace that you are allowed to do it.

And it´s the same SCAM on both Aliexpress and Alibaba

I do believe that Trust pilot and Google should /could include a ZERO star  rating - because then these 2 operators would be called in their bluff. 

My best advice - boy-cut it all until they start showing real pictures with real prices ... and honest transport service.. so they promise free transport.. until you order it...oooh it is so heavy .... bla. bla. bla. So now the prices has doubled and you need to buy containers of a product .... of which you have no belief in what they are offering.
